title: Color Profile Pattern
text: Automatic Automatically configures the best color profile pattern depending on the appearance of the document to print. Automatic (Brighter) Automatically configures the best color profile pattern to be brighter. Automatic (Darker) Automatically configures the best color profile pattern to be darker. Text Optimizes the colors for text. Text (Brighter) Optimizes the colors for text to be brighter. Text (Darker) Optimizes the colors for text to be darker. Photographic Enhances mid-tone colors similar to those seen in photographs. Photographic (Brighter) Enhances mid-tone colors, similar to those seen in photographs, to be brighter. Photographic (Darker) Enhances mid-tone colors, similar to those seen in photographs, to be darker. Presentation Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics. This setting is best for printing tables, graphs, and presentation materials that contain color. Presentation (Brighter) Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics to be brighter. Presentation (Darker) Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics to be darker. CAD Enhances reproduction of even colors that are true to the original. POP Display Prints the color red more vividly. It is an optimal setting for the POP display. Color Variation 1 (Bright/Yellow) Enhances colors suitable for portraits. Color Variation 2 (Dark/Red) Enhances colors suitable for portraits or food. Color Variation 3 (Darker/Blue) Prints the color blue more vividly. Suitable for landscapes. Color Variation 4 (Dark/Yellow) Enhances dark-tone colors over the whole area. Color Variation 5 (Brighter/Red) Enhances bright-tone colors over the whole area. Color Variation 6 (Brighter/Yellow) Enhances brightness and contrast over the whole area. Color Variation 7 (Darker/Red) Enhances dark-tone colors and contrast over the whole area. Off Prints colors without modification. Use ICM Corrects colors using the Windows ICM function. Expand Gray Recognition Checks every pixel and prints gray pixels (when the values of RGB are equal or nearly equal) using black toner only. This setting is available only if you have selected K: Expand Gray Recognition in the Gray Reproduction: list. Barrier-free Color Management Converts the colors used in documents to the barrier-free colors applicable to Color Universal Design (CUD). This setting is available only if you have selected On in the Barrier-free Color Management: list.

title: Dithering Pattern
text: Automatic Automatically configures the best dithering method depending on the appearance of the document to print. Photographic Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for photographs. Text Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for text. Thin lines Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for thin lines. CAD Performs dithering using a pattern that enhances reproduction of fine lines.

title: Using Help
text: This system is designed to provide more information about each of the printer features supported by the RPCS printer driver. Displaying Help for the Printer Driver Click the Help button in the dialog box to display an explanation of the dialog box. Click the Contents tab in the left window to display the table of contents. From here you can view each Help topic. Select the item whose Help topics you want to see, and then press the F1 key. If a question mark button is displayed in the upper right corner of the printing preferences dialog box, click it. Your mouse's pointer will change to a question mark . Move this question mark over the item whose Help information you want to view, and then left-click to display the Help information. Printing Help Topics To print the currently displayed Help topic, click the Print button at the top. Note for Printer Driver Tabs and Dialog Boxes The Accessories and Advanced Options tabs are not available in the printing preferences dialog box when accessing from the application's Print dialog box. When you make settings on the Accessories and Advanced Options tabs, you must log on as a member of the Administrators or Power Users group.

title: About Dialog Box
text: Displays copyright and version information. Save Driver Settings... Saves the current driver settings and details of the operating system, driver version, and driver modules (version and date) as a file. OK Closes the dialog box.

title: Accessories Tab
text: Use this tab to configure the options installed on the printer, and register the available input trays and paper sizes. Registration of paper sizes enables you to search for a printer loaded with paper of a desired size using the Active Directory function of Windows. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Machine Image Displays the printer configuration as an image. Options Select the options installed on the printer. Whenever an option is added, select it in the Options group. Even if an option is physically installed, it will not be available for printing unless it is selected on this tab. The Punch Unit: list is available when an optional finisher with punch unit is installed and selected. Select a type of punch unit in the list. Depending on the type of unit selected, available punching positions will vary. Note: If the settings configured on this tab do not match the physical configuration of the printer, you may get unexpected print results. Total Memory: Specify the total size that is currently installed on the printer. Or simply clicking Update Now configures the current size of memory if the printer has bidirectional communication. Input Tray Settings Change Input Tray Settings... Opens the Change Input Tray Settings dialog box, where you can configure settings related to the paper in the paper trays. Input Tray Settings List: Lists input trays and the size of paper loaded. Automatically Update Printer Information Whenever you open the printer properties dialog box, this function queries the printer for its configuration and automatically obtains information about any options installed on the printer. Note: This function is available only if bidirectional communication between the printer and computer is established by network or direct cable connection. For more information about bidirectional communication, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Update Now Queries the printer for its configuration and automatically obtains information about any options installed on the printer. Note: This function is available only if bidirectional communication between the printer and computer is established by network or direct cable connection. For more information about bidirectional communication, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this tab to the default settings.

title: Advanced Options Tab
text: Use this tab to configure further advanced options for printing. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Manage One Click Presets Manage... Opens the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box to specify a one click preset name and comment, or change the display order. You can also share registered one click presets among users and delete existing one click presets. Do not Allow User to Register Preset Prohibits users from registering one click presets. When users open Frequently Used Settings Tab or Detailed Settings Tab, Register Current Settings... is grayed out, users cannot register new one click presets. Users cannot specify a one click preset name and comment, nor change the display order in the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box (Printing Preferences). Do not allow changing the display order in One Click Preset List Prohibits users from changing the order of the system-provided and shared one click presets. Users can only change the order of the one click presets they register. If you clear the check box, you can change the order of all kinds of one click presets. User Authentication... Open the User Authentication dialog box to set the user authentication settings. Job Type/Code Dialog Settings... Open the Job Type/Code Dialog Settings dialog box to set the printing method for printing. Security Settings... Open the Security Settings dialog box to set whether to encrypt print data. Increase Auto-keep Settings for Applications Select the check box to apply the print settings of the previous sheet when using an application such as Microsoft® Excel®. Make the print settings for the first of the four sheets of data. These print settings are applied to the remaining three sheets. Collate by Device If you cannot use the collate function because the optional hard disk or additional memory is not installed in the printer, clear this check box to have the prints sorted into sets according to the application collate settings. Notify application that both dmPaperLength and dmPaperWidth are not supported Select the check box to turn off dmPaperLength and dmPaperWidth for DC_FIELDS and dmFields in the driver. Register Custom Paper Size... Opens the Register Custom Paper Size dialog box, where you can register custom paper sizes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this tab to the default settings.

title: Background Numbering Details Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to specify the details of the background numbering for confidential documents, for example. An individual watermark number is printed on each copy. Recording the number to be distributed among other users can prevent unauthorized copies. Background Numbering Print Image Displays an image of the background numbering print. Note: The displayed image may differ from actual prints. Size: Select the size for the background numbering text. Density: Select the density for the background numbering text. Color: Select the color for the background numbering text. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Start Number: Enter the start number for numbering. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Basic
text: Use this menu to make basic print settings. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Orientation Select the orientation of your document. Color/ Black and White: Select whether the document is printed in color or black and white. Note: Color images will be printed using CMYK toner: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, and Black. CMY are the three primary subtractive colors. If you want to adjust the print color, use the settings on the Print Quality:Standard and/or Print Quality:Advanced menus. For two-color printing, select Color . Configure two-color printing in the Two-color: list on the Print Quality:Standard menu. Rotate by 180 Degrees Prints the image upside down. For example, use this function if paper loaded in a tray has the top and bottom fixed, and printing with the paper in that direction would otherwise make the image upside-down. Copies: Enter the number of copies. Depending on the printer you use, the maximum number of copies may be different. Document Size: Select the paper size set in the application. Most applications will specify the paper size automatically, so this setting might not be necessary. To specify a non-standard paper size, select a registered custom paper size. Alternatively, enter the paper size in the Custom Paper Size dialog box, which is accessible through Custom Paper Size... . Note: If you select a document size conflicting with the size set in your application, the document may be printed with the one specified in the application. Custom Paper Size 1 to Custom Paper Size 10 can be registered on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. Depending on the printer you are using, up to 100 custom paper sizes can be registered. Custom Paper Size... Opens the Custom Paper Size dialog box, where you can specify a non-standard paper size. Printing on Custom Size Paper Reduce/Enlarge: You can reduce or enlarge the image. Reducing and Enlarging a Document Size Off Do not reduce or enlarge the image. Fit to Print Size The document is automatically reduced or enlarged to fit the paper size selected in the Print On: list. Zoom Select it if you want to reduce or enlarge the image manually. Directional Magnification Enter reduction and enlargement ratios for the vertical and horizontal directions separately. Zoom: When you want to zoom in or out the image to print, define the value in % in the spin box. The original size of the document is able to shrink or enlarge from 25% to 400% when printed. Note: This function is available only if Zoom is selected for Reduce/Enlarge: . Vertical: / Horizontal: Enter reduction and enlargement ratios for the vertical and horizontal directions separately by specifying a percentage between 25 and 400% (adjustable in steps of 1%). Print On: When you want to print the document on a different size paper than the document size specified in the Document Size: list, select the physical paper size from the list. If you do not want to change the print size, you may select Same as Original Size .

title: Collate Details Dialog Box
text: Select the collate type applied when the collate function is selected. Note that the collate types that are available will vary depending on your printer or the configuration. Collate Type: Collate Print sets are all delivered in the same orientation. Rotating Collate Every other print set is rotated by 90 degrees and delivered to the output tray. Rotating Collate is available only if paper of the same size is loaded in in the trays (in portrait or landscape orientation). Note: If you specify a tray other than Auto Tray Select for the input tray, Rotating Collate is not available. Shift Collate Print sets are alternately shifted when delivered to the output tray. Stapled print sets are not shifted. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Configuration/About Tab
text: Specify the tab configuration. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Default Tab: Select the default tab which is displayed when you open a Printing Preferences screen. Default Menu for Detailed Settings: Select the default menu which is displayed when you open the Detailed Settings tab. One Click Preset List Type: Specify a view style when you open the Frequently Used Settings tab. Printer Properties Opens the printer properties dialog box. You can configure the options installed on the printer or manage one click presets on the Accessories and Advanced Options tabs of the printer properties dialog box. About Provides copyright and version information. Printer Diagnostic Correction Tool If the printer does not print, click this button to start the tool to diagnose and fix the problem. Web Image Monitor... Starts Web Image Monitor . Web Image Monitor allows you to check the printer's status, manage jobs, and change settings, via a Web browser. For details, see the Web Image Monitor Help. Note: This function is available only if your computer is connected to the printer by the standard TCP/IP (IPv4/IPv6), WSD (IPv4), IPP (IPv4), or Ridoc IO Navi (IPv4/IPv6/IPP) port. This function will be unavailable if the IPv6 address you specify includes a number following the % symbol at the end of the address (also known as the "zone identifier" or "scope ID"), or if your computer is connected to this machine through network printer sharing.

title: Printing a Document Using the Colors Applicable to Color Universal Design
text: This function allows you to convert the colors used in a document to the barrier-free colors applicable to Color Universal Design (CUD). You can print the document in the converted colors so that people with various types of color vision can distinguish the colors easily. Note: This function is available only for color printers. The color tone of the print result might differ considerably from the color tone of the original. If you select this function, Barrier-free Color Management is automatically selected for Color Profile: on the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Barrier-free Color Management: list, select On . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Custom Paper Size Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box for specifying non-standard paper sizes. To access it, click Custom Paper Size... on the Basic menu. The graphic illustrates which dimension is width " A ", and which dimension is length " B " in relation to the feed direction. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the units of measurement. Size Width: Enter the size of the paper edge (A) that is vertical relative to the feed direction of the printer. Length: Enter the size of the paper edge (B) that is horizontal relative to the feed direction of the printer. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Detailed Settings Tab
text: Use this tab to set details of printing. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Current Setting Print Image Displays a preview image of how the current settings affect the document when it is printed. Setting Icons Current settings are displayed using icons. Move your mouse's pointer over icons to see the details. Document Size: / Print On: / Reduce/Enlarge: Displays the document size, paper size, and Reduce/Enlarge settings of the current printer. Settings Summary Opens the Settings Summary dialog box. In the Settings List tab, shows the details of current settings. In the Tray List tab, shows the list of tray settings and displays the printer configuration as an image. Register Current Settings... Opens the Register Current Settings as One Click Preset dialog box. You can register the current settings as a one click preset with its name and comment. Menu: Select a menu. Job Setup Use this menu to make settings for print job. Basic Use this menu to make basic print settings. Paper Use this menu to make settings about paper sources. Cover/Slip/Designate Use this menu to make settings for covers, slip sheets, or chapter pages. 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet Use this menu to change the layout when printing, and set 2 sided printing. Imposition Use this menu to print a document using an imposition function. Output Settings Use this menu to make settings for the output tray or to specify how you want to have prints delivered to the output tray. Finishing Use this menu to specify how you want to finish prints after printing. Print Quality:Standard Use this menu to adjust the standard settings that can affect the output quality of the print jobs. Print Quality:Advanced Use this menu to adjust the advanced settings that can affect the output quality of the print jobs. Effects Use this menu to print a watermark text in a document. Driver Options Use this menu to provide functions concerned with controls peculiar to the driver.

title: Driver Encryption Key Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to enter the driver encryption key already set on the printer. The encryption function encrypts the login password when sending it to the printer. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Driver Encryption Key: Enter the driver encryption key already set on the printer. Reenter the Confirmation Key: Enter the driver encryption key again for confirmation. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet
text: Use this menu to change the layout when printing, and to set 2 sided printing. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Layout: Select the number of pages printed per sheet. Each document page to be printed on a sheet will be placed in the order selected in the Page Order: list. Printing Multiple Pages on a Sheet Page Order: Select a page layout when two pages or more per sheet is specified in Layout: . Draw Border Select the check box to print dotted separator lines for combined pages. Mixed Original Orientations... When applying layout-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, you can specify whether to print document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation rotated by 90 degrees or reduced in size without being rotated. 2 sided: Prints on both sides of sheets. Specify how you want to open the bound output in the list. Binding Margins... Open the Binding Margins for 2 sided Printing dialog box, where you can specify the binding margins for 2 sided printing. Booklet: Prints output so that you can fold it into a booklet. The pages of your document will be reduced in size and printed side by side, two on each side of each sheet of the original paper size specified in the application. For example, an A4 document will be printed as two A5 images on each side of each A4 sheet. Printing with a Layout Suitable for Making Booklets Note: There are only certain sizes of paper applicable for this function. To print at the same size as the original without size reduction, select a paper size that is double that of the original in the Print On: list on the Basic menu. Off Disables Booklet printing. Magazine Two document pages are reduced and printed side by side on each side of each sheet, and then the whole stack is folded in half, like a magazine. Mini Book Each sheet is folded in half separately, and then the folded sheets are stacked and bound. Page Order: Select a page layout when Magazine or Mini Book is specified in Booklet: . Mixed Original Orientations... When applying booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, you can specify the imposition method. Creep Adjustment... Prints the document with the creep adjustment function when Magazine is selected in Booklet: . Using the Creep Adjustment Function Do not [Fit to Print Size] auto. Select the check box to print original-size documents side by side at the center of the paper when Magazine is selected in Booklet: . Printable Area: If the same document is printed on different printers and results in a different number of pages being printed, adjust the printable area. If you want to print over the whole page surface, select Maximum . Note: The print inside the 5 mm (0.2 inches) margin around the paper edges might be of reduced quality. Set Image Position... Click to open the Set Image Position dialog box and then define the direction of the image position and the width of the margins. Do not Print Blank Pages Select the check box to leave blank pages unprinted.

title: Effects
text: Use this menu to specify whether or not to print a watermark on a document. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Unauthorized Copy Prevention Select the check box to set unauthorized copy prevention. Unauthorized Copy Prevention Type Select the prevention effect that you want from the list. Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern Use this function to embed a text and background pattern in confidential documents. If an unauthorized copy of the document is made, the background pattern and text will be clearly visible. This function makes it easy to identify unauthorized copies. Using Unauthorized Copy Prevention Function (Effects of Prevention for Pattern) Data Security for Copying If a document with an embedded copy guard pattern is copied, scanned, and/or stored in a machine with the Copy Data Security unit, the image of the page to be printed is destroyed, and turn the copy's color completely gray. Using Data Security for Copying Function (Destroy the Image and Print gray) Details... Opens the dialog box to specify the details of the unauthorized copy prevention. Background Numbering Select the checkbox to add background numbers when printing. Printing Control Numbers on the Background of Documents Details... Opens the dialog box to specify the details of the background numbering. Header/Footer Select the items that you want to print on header and footer. Details... Opens the Edit Header/Footer dialog box, where you can edit and create header and footer. Print Watermark Select the check box to print a watermark. Having Text Stamped on Prints Watermarks: Select the watermark that you want to print from the list. Edit... Opens the Edit Watermark dialog box, where you can edit and create watermarks. Add Overlay Select the check box to print a document with previously created Overlay Data superimposed. Overlay Data: Select the Overlay Setting that you want to use. Edit... Opens the Edit Overlay dialog box where you can edit and create Overlay Setting. Add Bitmap Select the check box to print a bitmap file (extension .bmp) as bitmap watermark. Bitmap: Select the bitmap watermark that you want to print from the list. Edit... Opens the Edit Bitmap dialog box where you can edit and create bitmap watermarks.

title: Finishing
text: Use this menu to specify how you want to finish prints after printing. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Staple: Select a stapling position. Note: Staple requires that the optional finisher be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. When this feature is enabled, prints are automatically collated. If the document being printed and stapled contains pages different in size or direction, those sheets printed might not get stapled in the job. Available staple positions vary depending on the punch position and the 2 sided setting. Documents may not be stapled at the slant angle, even when you select Top Left Slant or Top Right Slant . In such a case, the document will be stapled parallel to an edge of the paper. For more information about Staple, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Punch: Select a punching position. Punching positions in the list vary depending on the type of punch unit selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. Note: Punch requires that the optional finisher with punch unit be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. If the document being printed and punched contains pages different in size or direction, those sheets printed might not get punched in the job. Available punch positions vary depending on the stapling position and the 2 sided setting. Check these settings in advance. Available punch positions depend on the settings selected in Orientation and Print On: on the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu. Check these settings in advance. For more information about Punch, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Fold: Select the fold type that you want the optional folding unit, Z-folding unit, or supported finisher to apply. Fold types in the list vary depending on the type of folding unit selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. Printing with the Folding Unit Note: Folding or Z-folding is available only if the optional folding unit, Z-folding unit, or supported finisher is installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. Available fold type changes according to paper orientation, 2 sided setting, and stapling position. The folding function is not available for certain paper sizes and media types. For details, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Multi-sheet Fold Select the check box to use the multi-sheet folding function. If you enable this function, several sheets are folded at once. Note: Depending on the combination of fold type and print side that you have selected, this function might not be available. If the original contains more pages than can be folded at once, the job will be canceled. For details about the maximum number of pages that can be folded at once, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Ring Binding: Select a ring binding position. The ring binding function punches holes in prints and binds them using a ring comb. You can also use the ring binding function to punch ring binding holes in prints but not bind them. Binding Documents by Ring Comb Note: Ring Binding requires that the optional ring binder be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab. Perfect Binding Select the check box to use the optional perfect binder for making perfect bound booklets. Binding Documents by Perfect Binding Note: For details about the supported paper types and sizes, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Details... Opens the Perfect Binding Details dialog box, where you can configure the settings for perfect binding. Fore Edge Cut If center stapling is selected for Staple: , select the check box to cut the fore edge. Details... Opens the Fore Edge Cut Details dialog box, where you can configure the settings for the cut length of the fore edge. Extended Option: Select the finishing method if you want to finish prints after printing by using the 3rd vender's finisher connected to the machine.

title: Change Input Tray Settings Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to configure the settings for paper loaded in the paper trays. Input Tray: Select an input tray. If you select an optionally installed tray, be sure to specify the tray in the Options group. Paper Size: Select a paper size for the tray you have selected in Input Tray: . Paper Type: Select a type of paper loaded in the tray. Note: If you select Plain & Recycled (Auto. for Postcard) , it is normally printed as plain paper/recycled paper. If the print paper size is postcard, print with a paper type suitable for postcards. Do not Use Auto Tray Select Select the check box if the selected paper tray is set as unavailable for the Auto Tray Select function at the printer. Paper Position Select the direction of paper loaded. Modify Input Tray/Paper Size Click to update Input Tray Settings List: with the information in Input Tray: , Paper Size: , Paper Type: and Paper Position . Input Tray Settings List: Lists input trays and the size of paper loaded. To add a new entry, select an input tray, paper size, paper type and paper position, and then click Modify Input Tray/Paper Size . OK Saves the entries and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Job Type Details Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to set a user ID, file name, password and user name for the print job. This dialog box is accessible by clicking Details... after selecting Job Type: on the Job Setup menu or on the Frequently Used Settings tab. Depending on the Job Type you selected, the setting items may vary. User ID: Select whether to create your own user ID or to use your Windows login name as your user ID. This ID is used to specify the file to be printed or deleted from the printer's control panel. It also identifies individual users in the job history. The user ID is required for all types of job except Normal Print and Document Server jobs. Create Own ID Specify a user ID of your choice in the Enter User ID: box. Windows Login Name Auto-specifies your Windows login name as your user ID. Note: If the number of characters in your Windows login name exceeds 20 single-byte characters, your user ID will only display up to 20 single-byte characters. Enter User ID: Enter the user ID using up to eight characters, which are alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, and 0-9) characters and symbols ('_', '.', '-', '/', and ':'). File Name: You can optionally set a file name for each file depending on your purpose. Enter a file name using up to 16 single-byte or 8 double-byte characters except double quotation mark. Note: This function is available only if you selected Hold Print , Stored Print , Stored Print (Shared) , Store and Print , Store and Print (Shared) , or Document Server in the Job Type: list. Password: Enter a password using 4 to 8 digits when you selected Locked Print in the Job Type: list. You can also enter a password optionally if you selected Stored Print , Stored Print (Shared) , Store and Print , Store and Print (Shared) , or Document Server in the Job Type: list. When Locked Print , Stored Print , or Stored Print (Shared) is selected and the encryption function is enabled, the input range is from 4 to 32 alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, and 0-9) characters. User Name: Enter a user name using up to 16 single-byte or 8 double-byte characters except double quotation marks. This is used to indicate to whom the file in the Document Server belongs. Set Print Time Select the check box to print a job at a specified time. Note: This function is available only if you selected Hold Print in the Job Type: list. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Folder Number: Enter a number for the folder where you want to store the document, using a value between 0 and 200. If you specify "0", the document will be stored in the Shared Folder . Note: This function is available only if you selected Document Server in the Job Type: list. Folder Password: If the folder is password-protected, enter the password. Note: This function is available only if you selected Document Server in the Job Type: list. OK Saves the entries and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Job Setup
text: Use this menu to make settings for print job. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Job Type: Select a type of print job. Normal Print The print job starts immediately after a print command is given. To optionally enter a user ID, click Details... . Sample Print Select to have only the first set of a multiple set print job printed so you can check the appearance before printing the remaining sets. The remaining sets can be printed or canceled from the printer's control panel. Printing a Single Sample Set before Remaining Sets Locked Print When you want to print something you do not want anyone else to see, you can be sure that the printer does not start printing until you are physically present at the printer and enter password on the printer's control panel. Avoiding Others Seeing Your Prints Hold Print The print job is sent to the printer and saved temporarily on the printer's hard disk. When the saved job is printed, the job is deleted from the printer's hard disk. You can also print it at a specified time. Printing Documents Later Stored Print The print job is sent to the printer and stored on the printer's hard disk. You can print the stored job as many times as you require until you delete the job from the printer's hard disk. If you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab of the printer properties dialog box, a document can be printed only by its creator after she/he has logged in through the control panel. Storing Documents on the Hard Disk Stored Print (Shared) This option is available when you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. If you select this option instead of Stored Print , any user with print privileges can print the job. Storing Documents on the Hard Disk Store and Print The print job is stored on the printer's hard disk and printed at the same time. You can reprint the stored job as many times as you require until you delete the job from the printer's hard disk. If you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab of the printer properties dialog box, a document can be printed only by its creator after she/he has logged in through the control panel. Storing Documents on the Printer and Printing them Store and Print (Shared) This option is available when you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. If you select this option instead of Store and Print , any user with print privileges can print the job. Storing Documents on the Printer and Printing them Document Server Select this to send a file to the document server. The file will be stored in the document server for future editing or printing. To optionally enter a user ID, file name, password, or user name for the file, click Details... . Using the Document Server Note: Depending on the printer you are using, custom paper size document files cannot be stored in the document server. When the file stored in the document server is printed, certain features settings need to be set on the printer's control panel. Save as Overlay Data Creates Overlay Data, an image that is superimposed onto a document you have created. Click the Details... button, and enter the file name and destination for the ".rpo" overlay data file. Overlaying Printing Documents with Data Store as Image Overlay Saves image overlay data in the printer so that the data is superimposed onto a document you have created. Click the Details... button, and enter the registration number and registration name for the image overlay data. Registering Image Overlay Details... Opens the Job Type Details dialog box to enter a user ID, file name, or password according to the job type. Classification Code: According to the usage purpose, you can set a classification code. Enter up to 32 alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, 0-9, '_', '-') characters. Registering a Classification Code User Code: Enter a user code using up to 8 digits. A user code identifies a group of users and allows you to check the number of sheets printed under each code. Registering User Code Authentication... Opens the Authentication dialog box, where you can enter the login user name and password already set on the printer or server for the user authentication. To make this button available, select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab in the printing properties dialog box. Using User Authentication Note: For details about user authentication, see the operating instructions provided with the printer.

title: Manage One Click Preset List Dialog Box (Printing Preferences)
text: You can change the one click preset display order, delete a one click preset, and change its name and comment. You can also load a printing preferences settings file as a one click preset and save a registered one click preset as a file. Note: You cannot change the names and comments of the system-provided one click presets. One Click Preset List: Displays the registered one click preset names, comments, and status in the list. Up Moves the one click preset display order up. Down Moves the one click preset display order down. Delete Deletes the selected one click preset. Import... You can load a printing preferences settings file provided by an administrator as a one click preset. Export... You can save a registered one click preset as a file. One Click Preset Name: You can change the name of the one click preset selected in the list. Comment: You can change the comment of the one click preset selected in the list. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Frequently Used Settings Tab
text: On the Frequently Used Settings tab, you can use one click presets, which are pre-registered print settings. Features of This Printer Driver Registering the settings you frequently use such as those specific to a certain use or client will prevent configuration errors or reduce operational time. General one click presets are available as defaults on the Frequently Used Settings tab. You can also make changes to basic print settings displayed under One Click Preset List: . We recommend registering up to 32 one click presets including system-provided presets. If more than 32 one click presets are registered, performance may be affected and proper operation is not guaranteed. Note: You cannot register new one click presets if the Administrator prohibits users from registering them. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Current Setting Print Image Displays a preview image of how the current settings affect the document when it is printed. Setting Icons Current settings are displayed using icons. Move your mouse's pointer over icons to see the details. Document Size: / Print On: / Reduce/Enlarge: Displays the document size, paper size, and Reduce/Enlarge settings of the current printer. Settings Summary Opens the Settings Summary dialog box. In the Settings List tab, shows the details of current settings. In the Tray List tab, shows the list of tray settings and displays the printer configuration as an image. Register Current Settings... Opens the Register Current Settings as One Click Preset dialog box. You can register the current settings as a one click preset with its name and comment. This function is unavailable if the current setting is the same as the registered one. One Click Preset List: Displays one click presets by icons or a list. You can specify a view style in the Configuration/About tab. One click preset icons or text lines lists with the icon are shared among users. Also, one click preset icons or text lines lists with the icon are user-specific (not shared). System-provided one click presets or text lines do not have the or icon. Specify the details of the one click preset you selected. Expand list >> / << Collapse list Specify whether to extend or collapse One Click Preset List: . Note: You can only configure the settings for Color/ Black and White: and Copies: if you extend the list. Manage... Opens the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box to specify a one click preset name and comment, or change the display order. You can also delete the existing one click preset, import or export from setting files. You cannot delete system-provided one click presets. Job Type: Select a type of print job. Normal Print The print job starts immediately after a print command is given. To optionally enter a user ID, click Details... . Sample Print Select to have only the first set of a multiple set print job printed so you can check the appearance before printing the remaining sets. The remaining sets can be printed or canceled from the printer's control panel. Printing a Single Sample Set before Remaining Sets Locked Print When you want to print something you do not want anyone else to see, you can be sure that the printer does not start printing until you are physically present at the printer and enter your password on the printer's control panel. Avoiding Others Seeing Your Prints Hold Print The print job is sent to the printer and saved temporarily on the printer's hard disk. When the saved job is printed, the job is deleted from the printer's hard disk. You can also print it at a specified time. Printing Documents Later Stored Print The print job is sent to the printer and stored on the printer's hard disk. You can print the stored job as many times as you require until you delete the job from the printer's hard disk. If you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab of the printer properties dialog box, a document can be printed only by its creator after she/he has logged in through the control panel. Storing Documents on the Hard Disk Stored Print (Shared) This option is available when you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. If you select this option instead of Stored Print any user with print privileges can print the job. Storing Documents on the Hard Disk Store and Print The print job is stored on the printer's hard disk and printed at the same time. You can reprint the stored job as many times as you require until you delete the job from the printer's hard disk. If you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab of the printer properties dialog box, a document can be printed only by its creator after she/he has logged in through the control panel. Storing Documents on the Printer and Printing them Store and Print (Shared) This option is available when you select the User Authentication check box on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. If you select this option instead of Store and Print , any user with print privileges can print the job. Storing Documents on the Printer and Printing them Document Server Select this to send a file to the document server. The file will be stored in the document server for future editing or printing. To optionally enter a user ID, file name, password, or user name for the file, click Details... . Using the Document Server Note: Depending on the printer you use, custom paper size document files cannot be stored in the document server. When the file stored in the document server is printed, certain features settings need to be set on the printer's control panel. Save as Overlay Data Creates Overlay Data, an image that is superimposed onto a document you have created. Click the Details... button, and enter the file name and destination for the ".rpo" overlay data file. Overlaying Printing Documents with Data Store as Image Overlay Saves image overlay data in the printer so that the data is superimposed onto a document you have created. Click the Details... button, and enter the registration number and registration name for the image overlay data. Registering Image Overlay Details... Opens the Job Type Details dialog box to enter a user ID, file name, or password according to the job type. Document Size: Select the paper size set in the application. The application software specifies the size so you usually do not need to specify any. Note: If you select Custom Paper Size , you must then specify the paper size in the Custom Paper Size dialog box, which is accessible through Custom Paper Size... on the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab, or Frequently Used Settings tab. Custom Paper Size 1 to Custom Paper Size 10 can be registered on the Advanced Options tab in the printer properties dialog box. Depending on the printer you are using, up to 100 custom paper sizes can be registered. Print On: When you want to print the document on a different size paper than the document size specified in the Document Size: list, select the physical paper size from the list. If you do not want to change the print size, you may select Same as Original Size . Orientation Select the orientation of your document. Custom Paper Size... Opens the Custom Paper Size dialog box, where you can specify a non-standard paper size. Printing on Custom Size Paper Paper Type: Specify the type of printing medium you want to use. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Note: If you select Plain & Recycled (Auto. for Postcard) , it is normally printed as plain paper/recycled paper. If the print paper size is postcard, print with a paper type suitable for postcards. Input Tray: Select an input tray. Note: If you cannot select the desired input tray, check that all installed options are configured on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. If you select Auto Tray Select , the printer uses paper from another input tray that contains paper of the same size and type if there is no more paper left in the current tray. Layout: Select the number of pages printed per sheet. Each document page to be printed on a sheet will be placed in the order selected in the Page Order: list. Printing Multiple Pages on a Sheet Page Order: Select a page layout when 2 pages or more per sheet is specified in Layout: . 2 sided: Prints on both sides of sheets. Specify how you want to open the bound output in the list. Booklet: Prints output so that you can fold it into a booklet. The pages of your document will be reduced in size and printed side by side, two on each side of each sheet of the original paper size specified in the application. For example, an A4 document will be printed as two A5 images on each side of each A4 sheet. Printing with a Layout Suitable for Making Booklets Note: There are only certain sizes of paper applicable for this function. To print at the same size as the original without size reduction, select a paper size that is double that of the original in the Print On: list. Off Disables Booklet printing. Magazine Two document pages are reduced and printed side by side on each side of each sheet, and then the whole stack is folded in half, like a magazine. Mini Book Each sheet is folded in half separately, and then the folded sheets are stacked and bound. Page Order: Select a page layout when Magazine or Mini Book is specified in the Booklet: list. Staple: Select a stapling position. Note: Staple requires that the optional finisher be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. When this feature is enabled, prints are automatically collated. If the document being printed and stapled contains pages different in size or direction, those sheets printed might not get stapled in the job. Available staple positions depend on the setting selected in the Punch: and 2 sided: lists. Documents may not be stapled at the slant angle, even when you select Top Left Slant or Top Right Slant . In such a case, the document will be stapled parallel to an edge of the paper. For more information about Staple, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Punch: Select a punching position. Punching positions in the list vary depending on the type of punch unit selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. Note: Punch requires that the optional finisher with punch unit be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. If the document being printed and punched contains pages different in size or direction, those sheets printed might not get punched in the job. Available punch positions depend on the settings selected in the Staple: and 2 sided: lists. Available punch positions depend on the settings selected in Orientation and Print On: . Check these settings in advance. For more information about Punch, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Color/ Black and White: Select whether the document is printed in color or black and white. Note: Color images will be printed using CMYK toner: Cyan, Magenta, Yellow, and Black. CMY are the three primary subtractive colors. If you want to adjust the print color, use the settings on the Print Quality:Standard and/or Print Quality:Advanced menus of the Detailed Settings tab. For two-color printing, select Color . Configure two-color printing in the Two-color: list on the Print Quality:Standard menu. Copies: Enter the number of copies. Depending on the printer you are using, the maximum number of copies may be different.

title: Paper
text: Use this menu to make settings about paper sources. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Input Tray: Select an input tray. Note: If you cannot select the desired input tray, check that all installed options are configured on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. If you select Auto Tray Select , the printer uses paper from another input tray that contains paper of the same size and type if there is no more paper left in the current tray. Position in bypass tray... Select the orientation of the paper placed on the bypass tray. Paper Type: Specify the type of printing medium you want to use. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Note: If you select Plain & Recycled (Auto. for Postcard) , it is normally printed as plain paper/recycled paper. If the print paper size is postcard, print with a paper type suitable for postcards. [Tab Stock] Printing Select this in order to print a portrait document with the tab on the right and a landscape document with the tab on the top. Shift Print Position for [Tab Stock] Prints the image by shifting the image toward the tab so that you can print on the tab and also have extra space on the opposite side for stapling or punching. Letterhead Setting: Specify whether or not to print using the letterhead setting. This function enables you to print correctly on paper that has a fixed print side or print direction such as letterhead paper, for example. Note: For details about loading in the paper tray paper that has a fixed print side or print direction, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Printer Default Follows the printer settings. Off Disables the letterhead printing. When two-sided printing with an odd paged job is enabled, letterhead paper might not be printed correctly. Auto Detect Performs the letterhead printing when paper that has a fixed print side or print direction is specified in Paper Type: . On (Always) Always performs the letterhead printing. Apply [Letterhead Setting] to 1 sided print Specify whether or not to apply the letterhead setting to one-sided printing. Apply this to one-sided printing to print on letterhead paper correctly.

title: Print Quality:Standard
text: Use this menu to adjust the standard settings that can affect the output quality of the print jobs. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Adjust Image Quality/Color Correct the image quality and color tone to make the optimum setting for printing. Standard Settings Select the type of your document to print it with optimal settings for the type. The available items vary depending on the printer you are using. Generic Documents Prints with settings suitable for a standard document, such as that generated by a wordprocessor or spreadsheet application. Photographic Prints with settings suitable for documents containing fine gradations in tone, such as photographs. Note: Depending on the application you are using, images and graphics might be printed in full color (CMYK), even in black and white documents. DTP Prints with settings suited to reproduction of graphics. Note: Depending on the application you are using, images and graphics might be printed in full color (CMYK), even in black and white documents. POP Display Prints the color red more vividly. It is an optimal setting for the POP display. CAD Enhances reproduction of fine colored lines, for example, when printing from CAD applications are performed. Advanced Settings Allows you to configure the image quality and color tone manually. Details... Open the Details dialog box and set the details. Resolution: Select a resolution. The higher resolution will result in better print quality but may cause printing to take longer. Note: Resolutions are listed in reverse order of quality (lowest first). If you print large-sized or high-resolution images, the printing might not be processed due to low memory. In this case, select a lower print resolution than the one you selected. Toner Saving: Select a toner saving mode. The available items vary depending on the printer you are using. Off Prints without toner saving mode. On Reduces the amount of toner used when printing is performed. Toner Saving 1 Reduces the amount of toner used when printing is performed. Toner Saving 2 Further reduces the amount of toner used when printing is performed (more reduced than when Toner Saving 1 is selected). While this increases the life of the toner cartridge, the output appears slightly lighter. Medium Light Reduces the amount of toner used when printing is performed. Light Further reduces the amount of toner used when printing is performed (more reduced than when Medium Light is selected). While this increases the life of the toner cartridge, the output appears slightly lighter. User Setting Allows you to make detailed settings in the Toner Save User Settings dialog box. Barrier-free Color Management: Specify whether to convert the colors used in documents to the barrier-free colors applicable to Color Universal Design (CUD). The color tone of the print result might differ considerably from the color tone of the original. Print Priority: Select the method you want to use for rendering bitmaps. When documents containing high resolution bitmap images are printed, printing takes longer due to the large amount of data that must be processed. Normal Prints with a balance of quality and speed. Quality Prints with quality as priority. Speed Printing is fast. High Speed Prints with the priority on print speed. Two-color: Prints in two colors. Select the combination of toner colors. This function is available only if Advanced Settings is selected in Adjust Image Quality/Color . Printing in Two Colors

title: Register Custom Paper Size Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to register custom paper sizes. Up to ten custom paper sizes can be registered. Depending on the printer you are using, up to 100 custom paper sizes can be registered. The graphic illustrates which dimension is width " A ", and which dimension is length " B " in relation to the feed direction. Custom Paper Size List: Displays the registered custom paper names and sizes. Edit Make settings for custom paper sizes. Name: In Custom Paper Size List: , select an unused name, and then change it as necessary. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the units of measurement. Width: Enter the size of the paper edge (A) that is vertical relative to the feed direction of the printer. Length: Enter the size of the paper edge (B) that is horizontal relative to the feed direction of the printer. Modify Click to update the Custom Paper Size List: with the settings specified here. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Settings Summary Dialog Box
text: Displays a settings summary using a list and an image of the printer. Settings List Tab Expand Expands the settings summary list. Collapse Collapses the expanded list. List: Displays a list of the current print settings. Tray List Tab Machine Image Displays the selected tray as an image. The currently selected input tray is framed in blue, and the output tray is marked with a blue triangle. Note: When Auto Tray Select or Printer Default is selected, these marks are not displayed. Selected Tray List: Displays the input and output trays information. OK Closes the dialog box.

title: Setting Up Options
text: Even if options are physically installed in the printer, they cannot be used unless they are configured in the properties dialog box. After installing or uninstalling options, always update the option configuration. If bidirectional communication is operating between the printer and computer, open the printer properties dialog box or click Update Now on the Accessories tab to obtain updates on option configuration automatically. When the Automatically Update Printer Information check box is selected, you can obtain updates on option configuration automatically, simply by opening the printer properties dialog box. If bidirectional communication is not operating, you must update option configuration manually. Note: If you do not log on as a member of the Administrators or Power Users group, the settings on the Accessories tab are unavailable. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Updating the Option Configuration Manually (When Bidirectional Communication Is Not Operating) In the Devices and Printers window, open the printer properties dialog box. Click the Accessories tab. In the Options area, select check boxes of the options installed. In the Punch Unit: list, select the type of the punch unit that is installed. In the Total Memory: list, select the size of the memory that is installed in the printer. In the Input Tray Settings area, click the Change Input Tray Settings... button to open the dialog box. In the Input Tray: list, select the input tray where the paper is loaded. In the Paper Size: list, select the size of the paper loaded. In the Paper Type: list, select the type of paper loaded. If the selected input tray is set as unavailable for the Auto Tray Select function at the printer, select the Do not Use Auto Tray Select check box. In the Paper Position area, select the direction of the paper loaded. Click the Modify Input Tray/Paper Size button to update or add the information in Input Tray: , Paper Size: and Paper Type: to Input Tray Settings List: . After configuring all paper trays, click OK to close the dialog box. Click OK to close the printer properties dialog box.

title: Fore Edge Cut Details Dialog Box
text: This function allows you to cut the fore edge when 2 at Center is selected for Staple: . Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Adjust Fore Edge Cut Position: Specify the cut length of the fore edge. You can adjust the cut size in 0.01 inch or 0.1 mm increments. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the measurement unit. OK Saves the entries and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Edit Watermark Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to edit and create watermarks. Note: You cannot update or delete system-provided watermarks. Watermark Image Displays an image of the watermark as it appears on the page. Note: The displayed watermark image may differ from actual prints. Watermarks: Select the watermark that you want to edit or delete from the list. Delete Deletes the current watermark. Edit Use the following settings to control the appearance of the watermark. Name: Enter a name for the watermark. Text: Enter the watermark text. Font: Select the font type for the watermark text. Font Style: Select the font style for the watermark text. Color: Select the color for the watermark text. With black and white printing, the density of gray color changes. Frame/Outline: Select an ornament of font style. Rectangle frames the text with a rectangle. Circle frames the text with a circle. Outlined prints the text in outline form. Size: Specify a value in this spin box to adjust the size of the current watermark. Angle: Specify a value in this spin box to rotate the watermark about its central point. Density: Specify a value in this spin box to adjust the density of the current watermark. Add Adds an edited watermark as a new watermark to the list. Update Saves the changes after editing a watermark. Position: Select a printing position where you want to print a watermark. First Page Only Prints the watermark on the first page only. Opaque Makes the watermark opaque. The image under the watermark will not be visible. Repeat Prints watermarks repeatedly from the top left of the page. Per Original Page Print watermark on each original page even when Layout or Booklet setting is applied. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Having Text Stamped on Prints

title: Printing the Back Cover on a Different Type of Paper
text: Use the following procedure to have the last sheet printed on a different type of paper (for example, paper from a different paper tray) from the other pages. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Cover/Slip/Designate menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Back Cover check box, and then select the paper tray loaded with paper for the back cover sheet in the Input Tray: list. Depending on the printer you use, the input tray selected for the front cover may be always used for the last sheet. In this case, the Input Tray: list is unavailable. In the Print Mode: list, select the print mode to use when printing the back cover sheet. Back cover sheet not printed on is not included in the print count. Specify the type of printing medium you want to use in the Paper Type in Bypass Tray dialog box when using bypass tray paper as the back cover sheet. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing Control Numbers on the Background of Documents
text: Use this function to add background numbers when printing confidential documents, for example. An individual watermark number is printed on each copy. Recording the number to be distributed among other users can prevent unauthorized copies. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Background Numbering check box. Click Details... to open the Background Numbering Details dialog box. Specify the size, density, and color from Size: , Density: and Color: . Color: is available only for color printers. In the Start Number: box, enter the start number for numbering. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Adjusting Black Printing Quality
text: Use the following procedure to adjust black printing quality. Printing Gray Scale in Black and White or in Full Colors Selecting to Have Text Printed in Black Overprinting Black on a Background Color (Black over print) Printing Gray Scale in Black and White or in Full Colors Select black and white or full color to print gray scale. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color . Click the Details... button to open the Details dialog box and click the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. In the Gray Reproduction: list, select a printing method for gray scale. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job. Selecting to Have Text Printed in Black This method applies when printing colored text. Use this function to have colored text printed in black: for example, if text clearly visible on the computer screen appears faint when printed. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Advanced menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Print All Text as Black check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job. Overprinting Black on a Background Color (Black Over Print) This function allows black printing on a colored background and helps prevent misregistration. Use this function if your document features black graphics and/or text on a colored background. Note: This function is available only for color printers. When this function is selected, black and gray areas might be printed with CMYK toner, regardless of the setting specified for Gray Reproduction: . Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Advanced menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Black Over Print check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job.

title: Printing with a Layout Suitable for Making Booklets
text: Use the following procedure to print on both sides of sheets using a layout suitable for booklets. Two formats are available. Magazine : the whole stack is folded in half in a similar way to a magazine. Mini Book : each sheet is folded in half separately, and then the folded sheets are stacked and bound. The pages of your document will be reduced in size and printed side by side, two on each side of each sheet of the original paper size specified in the application. For example, an A4 document will be printed as two A5 images on each side of each A4 sheet. Similarly a Letter size document will be printed as two 5.5" x 8.5" images on each side of each Letter size sheet. The whole stack is folded in half, like a magazine. If you use the Booklet function and the Layout function together, you will be able to reduce the printing cost. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Magazine: Mini Book: Note: Depending on the printer you are using, it is required that the duplex unit be installed. To print at the same as the original without size reduction, select a paper size that is double that of the original in the Print On: list on the Basic menu. You can also specify it on the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select Magazine or Mini Book in the Booklet: list. Click the << Collapse list button if the Booklet: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. Select a page layout in the Page Order: list. Configure the setting for printing mixed orientation documents and if necessary, select a layout type in the Layout: list, or select the Do not [Fit to Print Size] auto. check box. Open the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab if the Frequently Used Settings tab is displayed. Click the Mixed Original Orientations... button to open the dialog box. For Rotate Mixed Original Orientation of the Output Settings menu, select Printer Defaults . Specify whether to print document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation rotated by 90 degrees or reduced in size without being rotated. Click OK to close the dialog box. Printing Multiple Pages on a Sheet If you select Magazine , configure Creep Adjustment... if necessary. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Correcting the Hue of the Digital Photos
text: This describes how to correct the hue of photos taken with a digital camera. If there are extreme light and shade differences between the object and background, the object may be too dark or too light. This function is effective for those types of photos. Note: This function is available only with color printers. This function may not be effective for all image data. Exposure Exposure refers to the levels of light in which the photo was taken. If there are extreme light and shade differences between the object and background, the object may be under exposed (too dark) or over exposed (too light). Display photo data taken with a digital camera in an application. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Print Quality:Advanced menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Adjust Photographs check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Using Designate/Chapter Function
text: Use the following procedure to divide a document into chapters and print the first page of each chapter on different paper. You can also specify a special print mode for the first page of each chapter. (Designate/Chapter) In addition, you can print the selected pages on different paper. (Designated Sheet Print) Depending on the printer you use, this function may not be available. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Changing the Print Mode for the First Page of Each Chapter Create a document containing several chapters in your application and open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Cover/Slip/Designate menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Designate/Chapter check box. Click Details... . The Designate/Chapter Details dialog box appears. In Page Number: , enter the page number on which a new chapter begins. You can specify multiple page numbers for multiple new chapters by inserting commas between the page numbers. If you use the application to configure print settings such as page range, odd/even pages only, or page layout, it is likely that this function's page numbering will be affected. For instance, if the document contains 60 pages but in the application you have specified the page range as 41 to 60, the printer will print pages 1 to 20. In the Print Mode: list, select the print mode for the page specified in Page Number: . In the Input Tray: list, select the input tray containing the media type to use for the chapter page. Specify the type of printing medium you want to use in Paper Type in Bypass Tray: when using bypass tray paper as the chapter page. Click Add to add your definitions of Page Number: , Print Mode: , and Input Tray: to Designate/Chapter Settings List: . If necessary, make settings for other chapters. The maximum numbers of chapter covers you can specify differs depending on the printer you are using. When you have completed defining all chapter pages, review the lists in Designate/Chapter Settings List: . To make modifications, select the item and make corrections in the settings. Click Modify after completing the corrections. To delete an unnecessary item, click Delete after selecting the one in the list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Printing the Selected Pages on Different Paper Note: Depending on the printer you use, the Designate/Chapter function is unavailable. Create a document containing several chapters in your application and open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Cover/Slip/Designate menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Designate/Chapter check box. Click Details... . The Designate/Chapter Details dialog box appears. In Page Number: , enter the range of pages to specify a new chapter by inserting a hyphen between the page numbers. You can specify multiple page numbers for multiple new chapters by inserting commas between the page numbers. If you use the application to configure print settings such as page range, odd/even pages only, or page layout, it is likely that this function's page numbering will be affected. For instance, if the document contains 60 pages but in the application you have specified the page range as 41 to 60, the printer will print pages 1 to 20. In the Print Mode: list, select Designated Sheet Print . In the Input Tray: list, select the input tray containing the media type to use for the specified range of pages. Specify the type of printing medium you want to use in Paper Type in Bypass Tray: when using bypass tray paper for the specified range of pages. Click Add to add your definitions of Page Number: , Print Mode: , and Input Tray: to Designate/Chapter Settings List: . If necessary, make settings for other chapters. The maximum numbers of chapters you can specify differs depending on the printer you are using. When you have completed defining all chapter pages, review the lists in Designate/Chapter Settings List: . To make modifications, select the item and make corrections in the settings. Click Modify after completing the corrections. To delete an unnecessary item, click Delete after selecting the one in the list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Having Prints Sorted
text: When printing multiple sets of documents such as meeting materials, use the Collate function to have the prints sorted into sets. Note: If you select Application Collate with Layout or 2 sided printing, depending on the application used, problems such as the first and last page being printed on the same sheet might occur since document separation might not be correctly detected. In this case, select Printer Collate . If you select Printer Collate , the amount of data passed to the printer is reduced compared to when using an application's collate function, which might result in faster printing. For example, if you are printing three sets of a two page document and the application's collate function is used, six pages of data may be sent to the printer depending on the application used. If the printer driver's collate function is used, only two pages of data (P1, P2) is sent to the printer which then generates the remaining sets (P1, P2, P1, P2). To apply stacking options, select Application Collate and set the application's collate function to "OFF" in the Print dialog box. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may require an additional memory or the optional hard disk to be installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Copies: box, enter the number of copies you want to print. If the Frequently Used Settings tab is open, click the Detailed Settings tab. Click the Output Settings menu, select Printer Collate in the Collate: list. Click Collate Details... to select the collate type you require. Depending on the printer you are using, Rotating Collate and Shift Collate might not be available. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Changing the Color Profiling Pattern
text: Colors on the display are produced using the three colors of RGB, but colors in print are composed of the four colors of CMYK. For printing, RGB color must be converted to CMYK color. When converting the color, you can adjust the color tones by changing the color profiling pattern. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color . Click the Details... button to open the Details dialog box and click the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. In the Color Profile: list, select a color profile pattern . If you select User Setting , click the Details... button to open the Color Profile Details dialog box.
