Make detailed color profile settings for each element of your document ( Text: , Graphic: , and Photo: ). Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Adding a Color Profile You can add the new color profile provided by the developer to the list and use it. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Driver Options menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Click the Color Profile Settings... button to open the dialog box. In the Name: box, enter a name. If you want to edit an existing color profile, select the color profile pattern in the Color Profile: list. In Path/File Name: or Browse... , specify the path name and file name of the color profile data to be used. Click Add or Update to save. If you click Update , the dialog box to confirm whether or not to save the change appears. Click OK to close the dialog box. In the Color Profile: list, select the color profile pattern you added to the list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Registering Custom Paper Sizes
text: Use the following procedure to register a frequently used custom paper size. Note: Up to ten custom paper sizes can be registered. Depending on the printer you are using, up to 100 custom paper sizes can be registered. This setting cannot be selected from the printer properties dialog box when opened from an application. In the Devices and Printers window, open the printer properties dialog box. Click the Advanced Options tab. Click the Register Custom Paper Size... button to open the dialog box. In Custom Paper Size List: , select an unused size or the size you want to change. If necessary, in the Name: box, change the name for this size using up to 24 characters. Enter the length and width of the paper as seen in the graphic. In Width: , enter the size of the paper edge that is vertical relative to feed direction. In Length: , enter the size of the paper edge that is horizontal relative to feed direction. Click the Modify button to update Custom Paper Size List: with information in the Edit area. Click OK to close the dialog box. Click OK to close the printer properties dialog box.

title: Changing the Dithering Pattern
text: Dithering is a technique where tiny dots are printed in patterns in order to create the illusion of tones and colors that are theoretically impossible to reproduce. You can change the method used to render these patterns from the original data by following these steps. Select a pattern that matches the actual print image. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color . Click the Details... button to open the Details dialog box and click the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. In the Dithering: list, select the dithering pattern most suitable for the image. Make detailed dithering settings for each element of your document ( Text: , Graphic: , and Photo: ). Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Using the Document Server
text: If the printer is equipped with the document server inside, document data can be stored in the document server for printing. The document server stores documents data for later printing. The data can be combined and finishing such as stapling and punching can be specified when printing. Even document data from different computers or document data scanned from a scanner can be combined. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: You can optionally set user ID, file name, password, and user name for each file depending on your purpose. Depending on the printer you are using, custom paper size document files cannot be stored in the document server. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Job Type: list, select Document Server and click Details... to open the Job Type Details dialog box. Click the << Collapse list button if the Job Type: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. In the User ID: list, select a user ID type. If you select Create Own ID , enter a user ID in the Enter User ID: box using up to eight characters, which are alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, and 0-9) characters and symbols ('_', '.', '-', '/', and ':'). If you select Windows Login Name , the user ID may appear as the following: If the number of characters in your Windows login name exceeds 20 single-byte characters, your user ID will only display up to 20 single-byte characters. In the File Name: box, enter a file name using up to 16 characters except double quotation marks (optional). In the Password: box, enter a 4 to 8 digits password (optional). If a password is used for a file, it must be entered on the printer's control panel for editing or printing the file stored in the document server. In the User Name: box, enter a user name using up to 16 characters except double quotation marks (optional). In the Folder Number: box, enter the number for the folder where you store the document data. If you specify "0", the document will be stored in the Shared Folder . If the folder is password-protected, enter the password in the Folder Password: box. Click OK . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. When saving document data in the document server, there are some settings unavailable and those cannot be selected. If you want to change settings such as finishing, specify the settings when printing the document from the document server. Start the print job. The document is stored in the document server.

title: Printing on Both Sides of the Paper
text: Use the following procedure to print on both sides of the paper. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: Set the same direction as that set in the application. If not, printing will be performed without the correct binding position. Depending on the printer you are using, it is required that the duplex unit be installed. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Specify how you want to open the bound output in the 2 sided: list. Click the << Collapse list button if the 2 sided: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. Specify the binding margins as necessary. Open the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab if the Frequently Used Settings tab is displayed. Click Binding Margins... to open the Binding Margins for 2 sided Printing dialog box. Enter the respective widths of the front and back binding margins. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing Only the First Sheet on a Different Type of Paper
text: Use the following procedure to have the first sheet printed on a different type of paper (for example, paper from a different paper tray) from the other pages. Depending on the printer you use, this function may not be available. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Cover/Slip/Designate menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Front Cover check box, and then select the paper tray loaded with paper for the cover sheet in the Input Tray: list. In the Print Mode: list, select the print mode to use when printing the cover sheet. Cover sheet not printed on is not included in the print count. Specify the type of printing medium you want to use in the Paper Type in Bypass Tray dialog box when using bypass tray paper as the front cover sheet. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Using Data Security for Copying Function (Destroy the Image and Print Gray)
text: Use this function to embed a text and background pattern in confidential documents. If a document with an embedded copy guard pattern is copied, scanned, and/or stored in a machine with the Copy Data Security unit, the image of the page to be printed is destroyed, and replaced with a solid gray image. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: Use the Unauthorized Copy Prevention function to make the background pattern and text clearly visible when an unauthorized document is copied, scanned, printed, and/or stored in the machine. This function requires that the Copy Data Security unit be installed on the printer. Depending on the printer you are using, you may need an MFP that comes with the Copy Data Security unit. For details, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. If an unauthorized document is copied, scanned, printed, and/or stored in a machine without the Copy Data Security unit, a warning message will be printed on the printed copy instead of the copy's color being completely gray. For details about data security for copying function and effects, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Printing with this function takes longer than normal printing because more data is processed. Depending on the data security for copying settings, the driver's prevention pattern may be overwritten by the printer's pattern. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Unauthorized Copy Prevention check box. Select Data Security for Copying in Unauthorized Copy Prevention Type . Click Details... to open the Data Security for Copying Details dialog box. Select the text type for the prevention text in the list. If you select User Text in Text Type: list, enter a user text using up to 64 single-byte characters. To change the font, font style and font size, specify from Font: , Font Style: and Size: . To change the angle, specify a value in Angle: . Select a position to enter the prevention text in Position: . To repeat text, select the pattern in Repeat: . Specify the line spacing in Line Space: . To print the text in outline form, select the Outlined check box. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing Documents Later
text: If the hard disk is installed on the printer, you can store a document on the hard disk, and print it later. Hold Print enables you to store a print job on the hard disk, and print it later. After printing, the document data is deleted from the hard disk. You can also print it at a specified time. Note: You must set a user ID to use Hold Print. A file name is optional. The maximum number of jobs and pages the printer can store differs depending on the printer you use. For details, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Job Type: list, select Hold Print and click Details... to open the Job Type Details dialog box. Click the << Collapse list button if the Job Type: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. In the User ID: list, select a user ID type. If you select Create Own ID , enter a user ID in the Enter User ID: box using up to eight characters, which are alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, and 0-9) characters and symbols ('_', '.', '-', '/', and ':'). If you select Windows Login Name , the user ID may appear as the following: If the number of characters in your Windows login name exceeds 20 single-byte characters, your user ID will only display up to 20 single-byte characters. In the File Name: box, enter a file name using up to 16 single-byte or 8 double-byte characters except double quotation mark (optional). If necessary, select the Set Print Time check box and specify the print time. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Click OK . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job. The print job is sent to the printer and saved on the printer's hard disk. Initiate the print job from the printer's control panel. For more information about using the printer's control panel, see the operating instructions provided with the printer.

title: Using ICM
text: Color correction is available using the Windows ICM function. ICM is a color management system that adjusts colors between I/O devices. Use this function to produce print results with colors as close as possible to those shown on the display. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color . Click the Details... button to open the Details dialog box and click the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. In the Color Profile: list, select Use ICM . In the Color Profile Method: list, select By Printer Driver . In the ICM Intent: list, select the color image rendering method. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job.

title: Printing Multiple Pages on a Sheet
text: Use the following procedure to have several document pages arranged on each print. This function is called Layout. Note: When using Layout, a suitable reduction or enlargement ratio is selected automatically based upon the paper size and the number of sheets you want to fit on each page. For example, an A4 document would be reduced in order to fit 2 pages on each sheet of A4 paper. An A5 document would be printed with four A5 document pages fitted on each sheet of A3 paper. If the page orientation varies within a document, a page break will occur before a page where the orientation changes. If an equivalent function is available from your application, turn it off and use the printer driver function. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select a layout type in the Layout: list. Click the << Collapse list button if the Layout: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. In the Page Order: list, select the page order. Select the Draw Border check box on the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab if you want to print dotted separator lines for combined pages. When specifying the orientation of an original containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, click the Mixed Original Orientations... button on the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select Printer Defaults for Rotate Mixed Original Orientation on the Output Settings menu in advance. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Features of This Printer Driver
text: This printer driver incorporates new usability features that were designed to meet all your needs with flexibility, whether you are a novice or advanced user. Using One Click Presets One click presets are registered combinations of print settings. They allow you to avoid having to make multiple print settings every time you want to print a job, thereby reducing the chances of mistakes and misprints. We recommend you use one click presets if you want to apply consistent print settings to multiple jobs. Several general one click presets are available as defaults on the Frequently Used Settings tab. You can also make changes to the basic print settings displayed under One Click Preset List: . Registering One Click Presets Also, since one click presets can be saved and retrieved as printer settings files, they can be shared among users. One click presets allow users without detailed knowledge of the printer properties to take advantage of the printer's more advanced features. Loading a Printing Preferences Settings File as a One Click Preset You can register up to 32 one click presets including system-provided presets. If more than 32 one click presets are registered, performance may be affected and proper operation is not guaranteed. In a multi-user environment, a thin client environment, or a "Point and Print" environment, users can share one click presets registered by the Administrator. Users without detailed knowledge of the printer driver properties can utilize the printer's advanced features by using the one click presets registered by the Administrator. Sharing One Click Presets Changing Print Settings Frequently The Detailed Settings tab provides menus for detailed print settings. If you change print settings frequently for various jobs, or often print using different settings, you can use these menus to make the detailed print settings that you require. For your convenience, we recommend you use an existing one click preset as a basis for new settings. To do this, select a one click preset on the Frequently Used Settings tab, and then, using the Detailed Settings tab, change the settings of the selected one click preset as required. If necessary, you can then register these settings as a new one click preset. Registering One Click Presets

title: Deleting a One Click Preset
text: Follow these steps to delete a one click preset. Note: You can only delete one click presets with the icon. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click Manage... on the Frequently Used Settings tab. The Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Select the one click preset name which you want to delete, and then click Delete . You cannot delete the system-provided one click preset. When a confirmation message appears, click Yes . Click OK to close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box.

title: Saving a Registered One Click Preset as a File
text: Follow these steps to save printing preferences settings registered to a one click preset as a file. Note: The following features settings are not stored for one click presets. User ID , File Name , Password , User Name , Classification Code , User Code , Login User Name , Login Password , Folder Password , watermark items except Print Watermark (On/Off) and selected watermark name, overlay items except Add Overlay (On/Off) and selected overlay name, bitmap items except Add Bitmap (On/Off) and selected bitmap name, color profile items except selected color profile name. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click Manage... on the Frequently Used Settings tab. The Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Select the one click preset name which you want to save as a file, and then click Export... . The Save As dialog box appears. In the File name: box, enter the file name to save the settings. The file name extension is ".json". Click Save . The dialog box closes and the setting is saved. Click OK to close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box.

title: Loading a Printing Preferences Settings File as a One Click Preset
text: Follow these steps to load a printing preferences settings file as a one click preset. This file would be provided by an administrator, for example. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click Manage... on the Frequently Used Settings tab. The Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Click Import... . The Open dialog box appears. Select the file containing the printing preferences settings, and then click Open . The printing preferences settings file is loaded and the one click preset is registered. Click OK to close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box.

title: Changing a One Click Preset Name and Comment
text: Follow these steps to change the name and comment of a one click preset. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click Manage... on the Frequently Used Settings tab. The Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Select the one click preset name which you want to change in One Click Preset List: . You cannot change the name and comment of the system-provided one click preset. Change the one click preset name and comment in the boxes below. The name can be up to 128 single-byte or 64 double-byte characters. The comment can be up to 512 single-byte or 256 double-byte characters. You can insert line breaks. Make sure the name and comment have been changed in the list. Click OK to save the changes and close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box.

title: Registering One Click Presets
text: Follow these steps to register one click presets. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab, and then select a one click preset from One Click Preset List: upon which you want to base the new one click preset. Modify settings on this tab. As necessary, you can also modify settings on the Detailed Settings tab. The following features settings are not stored for one click presets. User ID , File Name , Password , User Name , Classification Code , User Code , Login User Name , Login Password , Folder Password , watermark items except Print Watermark (On/Off) and selected watermark name, overlay items except Add Overlay (On/Off) and selected overlay name, bitmap items except Add Bitmap (On/Off) and selected bitmap name, color profile items except selected color profile name. Click Register Current Settings... to open the dialog box. Enter a name and comment. The name can be up to 128 single-byte or 64 double-byte characters. The comment can be up to 512 single-byte or 256 double-byte characters. You can insert line breaks. Click OK to register the one click preset and close the dialog box. The icon is displayed on the registered one click preset.

title: Changing the One Click Preset Display Order
text: Follow these steps to change the one click preset display order. For optimal ease-of-use, change the order according to setting type and how often you use them. Note: You can only change the settings of one click presets with the icon depending on the setting for Do not allow changing the display order in One Click Preset List on the Advanced Options tab of the printer properties dialog box. Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click Manage... on the Frequently Used Settings tab. The Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Select the one click preset whose order you want to change, and then click Up or Down . Only one click presets with the icon are displayed in the list depending on the settings for Do not allow changing the display order in One Click Preset List on the Advanced Options tabs of the printer properties dialog box. Click OK to save the changes and close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box.

title: Sharing One Click Presets
text: In a multi-user environment, a thin client environment, or a "Point and Print" environment, users can share the one click presets registered by the Administrator. Note: To make this setting, you must be logged in as an Administrator. In the Devices and Printers window, open the printer properties dialog box. Click the Advanced Options tab. Click Manage... , and the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box appears. Select the one click preset name which you want to share, and then select the Share check box. If necessary, click Up or Down to change the display order of the one click presets. If necessary, change the one click preset name and comment in the boxes below. The name can be up to 128 single-byte or 64 double-byte characters. The comment can be up to 512 single-byte or 256 double-byte characters. You can insert line breaks. Make sure the settings have been changed in the list. If everything is correct, click OK to save the changes and close the Manage One Click Preset List dialog box. Click OK . The printer properties dialog box closes.

title: Binding Documents by Perfect Binding
text: If your printer is equipped with the perfect binder, the Perfect Binding function is available. Perfect binding is a binding method that applies heated glue to printed sheets to form a book block, encloses the book block in a cover sheet, and trims away excess paper to create neat edges. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: For details about perfect binding and supported paper types and sizes, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. On the Frequently Used Settings tab, specify the size of original and the paper source tray. You can also specify them on the Basic and Paper menus of the Detailed Settings tab. Click the Finishing menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Perfect Binding check box. Click Details... . The Perfect Binding Details dialog box appears. In the Binding Position: list, select a binding position. In the Binding Paper Source Tray: list, select a paper source tray for the cover sheet. In the Perfect Binding Cutting Options: list, select a cut method for the cover sheet. In the Adjust Image Position area, you can specify a distance by which you want to shift the print image on the book block pages. In the Adjust Cut Position area, specify the necessary settings according to the cutting method selected in the Perfect Binding Cutting Options: list. The shaded settings are unavailable. For details about Perfect Binding cutting options, see the Perfect Binding Details dialog box. Click OK to close the Perfect Binding Details dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Using Unauthorized Copy Prevention Function (Effects of Prevention for Pattern)
text: Use this function to embed a text and background pattern in confidential documents. If an unauthorized copy of the document is made, the background pattern and text will be clearly visible. This function makes it easy to identify unauthorized copies. If documents printed with Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern are copied, scanned, and/or stored, functions are disabled in order to prevent information leakage. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: If you want the document image to be replaced by a solid gray image when printed documents are scanned, copied, or sent to the Document Server without permission, use the Data Security for Copying function. For details about the unauthorized copy prevention function and effects, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Printing with this function takes longer than normal printing because more data is processed. Depending on the unauthorized copy prevention settings, the driver's prevention pattern may be overwritten by the printer's pattern. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Unauthorized Copy Prevention check box. Select Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern in Unauthorized Copy Prevention Type . Click Details... to open the Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern Details dialog box. Select the text type for the prevention text in the list. If you select User Text in Text Type: list, enter a user text using up to 64 single-byte characters. To change the font, font style and font size, specify from Font: , Font Style: and Size: . To change the angle, specify a value in Angle: . Select a position to enter the prevention text in Position: . To repeat text, select the pattern in Repeat: . Specify the line spacing in Line Space: . To print the text in outline form, select the Outlined check box. To use only the text pattern when printing with the unauthorized copy prevention, select the Text Only check box. To exchange the pattern of the text and the pattern of the background, select the Reverse Patterns (Text/Background) check box. Select the mask type for the background pattern in Mask Type: . Select the density and color of the prevention copy text/pattern in Density: and Color: . You can use only black for monochrome printers. To exclude the specified area from being printed with the pattern, select the No Pattern Area: check box. Specify the values for A:top , B:bttm , C:left , and D:right in mm. The specified range is 1-9999 mm. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing with Optimal Settings for Document
text: You do not need specialist knowledge of print quality to make the best settings for your document. Use the following procedure to print a document with the optimal settings for its type. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: If you select DTP or Photographic in the Standard Settings of the Adjust Image Quality/Color , depending on the application you are using, images and graphics might be printed in full color (CMYK), even in black and white documents. Characters may also be printed using full color (CMYK) instead of pure Black (K), as some applications send characters as image data to the RPCS driver. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Standard Settings of the Adjust Image Quality/Color , select the icon that matches the kind of document you want to print. If you select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color , you must then manually set Dithering: , Color Profile: , and Gray Reproduction: . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing in Color or Black and White
text: Use the following procedure to print a document in color or black and white. For greater darkness in black and white images, the use of Black and White printing is recommended. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Color/ Black and White: list, select Color or Black and White as necessary. If you want to adjust the print quality, click the Print Quality:Standard , Print Quality:Advanced menus on the Detailed Settings tab, and then configure the necessary settings. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing a Single Sample Set before Remaining Sets
text: If the hard disk is installed in the printer, you can use the Sample Print function. If you are printing multiple sets of a document, printing a sample set first allows you to verify whether the printout is satisfactory. If you are satisfied with the first set, you can start printing the remainders by entering your user ID on the printer's control panel. Conversely, if you are unsatisfied and want to make changes to the document, you can cancel printing the remaining sets from the printer's control panel. Note: A user ID must be set to use Sample Print. The maximum number of jobs and pages the printer can store differs depending on the printer you use. For details, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Job Type: list, select Sample Print and click Details... to open the Job Type Details dialog box. Click the << Collapse list button if the Job Type: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. In the User ID: list, select a user ID type. If you select Create Own ID , enter a user ID in the Enter User ID: box using up to eight characters, which are alphanumeric (a-z, A-Z, and 0-9) characters and symbols ('_', '.', '-', '/', and ':'). If you select Windows Login Name , the user ID may appear as the following: If the number of characters in your Windows login name exceeds 20 single-byte characters, your user ID will only display up to 20 single-byte characters. For more information about using the printer's control panel, see the operating instructions provided with the printer.

title: Changing the Print Resolution
text: Use the following procedure to change the print resolution for printers that support multiple resolutions. Resolution is measured in the number of dots that can be printed per inch, or dpi. The higher the value, the higher the resolution and detail in which the image is rendered. However, printing takes longer. For faster printing use lower resolutions. Note: If you print large-sized or high-resolution images, the printing might not be processed due to low memory. In this case, select a lower print resolution than the one you selected. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Resolution: list, select a resolution. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Starting Printing from the Last Page
text: Printing starts from the last page. Note: If the application you are using has a similar function, do not make settings with the application's function. If you use this function when applying 2 sided printing to a document with an odd number of pages, the blank last page will also be included in the print count. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Output Settings menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Reverse Order Printing check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Binding Documents by Ring Comb
text: If your printer has the Ring Binder installed, the Ring Binding function is available. The Ring Binding function punches holes in prints and binds them using a ring comb. This function can only punch ring binding holes in prints. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: For details about paper sizes and media types that can be used with this function, see the instructions provided with the printer. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Finishing menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Ring Binding: list, select the ring binding position. After making any additional settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Rotating the Image by 180 Degrees
text: Use the following procedure to have the image printed rotated by 180 degrees. For example, use this function if paper loaded in a tray has the top and bottom fixed, and printing with the paper in that direction would otherwise make the image upside-down. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Basic menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Rotate by 180 Degrees check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Storing Documents on the Hard Disk
text: If the hard disk is installed on the printer, you can store a document on the hard disk, and print it later. Data remains on the hard disk until it is deleted. title: Avoiding Others Seeing Your Prints
text: If the hard disk is installed in the printer, you can use the Locked Print function. Note: A user ID and password must be set to use Locked Print. The maximum number of jobs and pages the printer can store differs depending on the printer you use. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Job Type: list, select Locked Print and click Details... to open the Job Type Details dialog box. The print job is sent to the printer and saved on the printer's hard disk. Initiate the print job from the printer's control panel. For more information about using the printer's control panel, see the operating instructions provided with the printer.

title: Inserting Different Paper between Pages
text: Use the following procedure to have paper fed alternately one sheet at a time from two trays. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Stapling Prints
text: When a printer is equipped with a finisher, the printed documents can be stapled in individual sets. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Select the stapling position in the Staple: list. When this feature is in use, the printed document is collated automatically. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Saving on Toner When Printing
text: If your printer supports a toner saving function, this describes how you can save on toner. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Toner Saving: list, select On or specify a toner saving level. Available items might vary depending on your machine model. If you select User Setting , click the Toner Save User Settings... button to open the dialog box. Configure Text: , Graphics: , and Photograph: to specify the amount of toner used for each element, and then click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Having Text Stamped on Prints
text: Use the following procedure to have text stamped on prints. To create, edit, and delete a watermark, see the following procedures: Printing a Watermark Editing a Watermark/Creating a New Watermark Deleting a Watermark Note: You cannot update or delete system-provided watermarks. Printing a Watermark Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Print Watermark check box. Select a watermark in the Watermarks: list. To see the details of the watermark, click Edit . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Editing a Watermark/Creating a New Watermark Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Print Watermark check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. In the Watermarks: list, select the watermark that you want to edit. If you want to register a new watermark, enter a name for it in the Name: box. Enter the text in the Text: box. The text appears in the preview window. To change the font, font style and color, specify from the Font: , Font Style: , Color: , and Frame/Outline: lists. To change the text size, angle, and density, specify a value in the Size: , Angle: , and Density: boxes. Select a printing position where you want to print a watermark in the Position: list. To print the watermark on the first page only, select the First Page Only check box. To place the watermark over the image, select the Opaque check box. The image under the watermark will not be visible. To print the watermark repeatedly, select the Repeat check box. Click OK to close the dialog box. Deleting a Watermark Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Print Watermark check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. Select a watermark from the Watermarks: list, and then click Delete . A dialog box appears prompting for confirmation. Click Yes . Click OK to close the dialog box.

title: Checking the Printer's Status
text: You can start Web Image Monitor from this printer driver to check the printer's status, manage jobs, and change settings, via a Web browser. title: Applying the One Sheet Print Setting to Others
text: When you create several sheets of data in applications such as Microsoft® Excel® and want to print out all sheets using the same print settings, you can apply the print settings of the first sheet to the rest. By using this function, you need not to make print settings for the other sheets. Make the print settings for the first of the four sheets of data. title: Using User Authentication
text: If the user authentication settings have been made on the printer, you also need to make the user authentication settings on the printer driver. Depending on the printer you use, this function may not be available. What Is User Authentication? With user authentication, only users who are registered on the printer or server can print using the printer. You need to make the login user name and login password settings for a user to enable that user to print. Users who are not registered on the printer or server cannot use the printer. Follow the steps to utilize the User Authentication function. Note: For details about user authentication, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. When the user authentication function is used, the user code setting on the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab becomes invalid. In the Devices and Printers window, open the printer properties dialog box. On the Advanced Options tab, click User Authentication... to open the User Authentication dialog box. When you make settings on the Advanced Options tab, you must log on as a member of the Administrators or Power Users group. Select On for User Authentication . Select the check box for Display [Authentication] Dialog Before Printing or Display [Authentication] Dialog Before Printing for Windows Credentials . Select the Encrypt [Login Password] , enter the driver encryption key already set on the printer and click OK . Click OK to close the printer properties dialog box. In the Devices and Printers window, open the printing preferences dialog box. On the Basic tab, click Authentication... . The Authentication dialog box appears. Select a type of login user name, and then enter a login user name and password that is already set on the printer or server for user authentication. title: Changing Bitmap Printing Resolution and Speed
text: When printing documents that contain high resolution bitmap images, printing takes longer due to the larger amount of data that must be processed. By changing the method for bitmap rendering, you can specify whether to give priority to quality or speed . Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Print Priority: list, select an image processing priority. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Changing the Image Data Processing Method Depending on the application, there may be cases where printing takes a long time, or colors are not reproduced correctly. In this kind of situation, changing the image data processing method may rectify the problem. Since changing the image data processing method may cause printing not to function correctly with some applications, you should normally leave this option unselected. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Advanced menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Change Data Processing check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Registering Classification Code and User Code
text: Use the following procedure to register classification code and user code. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Job Setup menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the User Code: box, enter a user code using up to eight digits. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Driver Options
text: Use this menu to provide functions related to controls specific to the driver. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Spool Data in EMF Format Select the check box to set the spooling format to EMF. This will reduce the time the printer takes to release itself from the printing process. Changing the spooling format might also resolve print problems.
