Shift Load to Printer Maximizes the load share of the print process on the printer. Select this if the print process takes time and the computer has a low capacity to process the job. Restore Last Emulation Returns to the setting before the print job. Near Standard Size When a document is scanned for printing, its size might be detected as larger than the original and a printer error might occur. Select the check box to prevent this problem. Use Application Zoom Use the application's zoom. Select the check box when lines are not printed in Microsoft® or Excel® files. Always apply COLOR to dmColor setting for appLication When you perform black-and-white printing for color documents created by using Microsoft® PowerPoint® and so on, some objects are filled with black when printed. If this is the case, enable this function. You will obtain print results you require. Display Preview and Print Screen Select the check box to display the preview screen to check print previews. You can also change some of the settings on the screen. Note: This function may not be available in a "Point and Print" environment. Auto Reduce: Documents larger than the specified size can be automatically reduced and printed. For example, if you select A3 (297 x 420 mm) , an A2 size document will automatically be reduced to A3 and printed. If you select A4 (210 x 297 mm) , a document larger than A4 will automatically be reduced to A4 and printed. Color Profile: Add, edit or delete a color profile in the list. You can add the new color profile provided by the developer to the list and use it.

title: Printing a Document Using Only Specific CMYK Colors
text: When you print a color document, usually the cyan, magenta, yellow, and black colors are used. However, you can choose to use only specific CMYK color(s) when printing. For example, you can use magenta and yellow for printing a document in red only, or magenta and cyan for blue only, or yellow and cyan for green only. As a result, printing costs will be reduced. Note: This function is available only for color printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality:Advanced menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the color or colors you want to use in the Separate into CMYK, then Print in Designated Color Only area. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job.

title: Paper Position in Bypass Tray Dialog Box
text: You can change the orientation of paper placed on the bypass tray. Set Paper Position in Bypass Tray To place paper in portrait orientation, select the Place as Portrait check box. For landscape orientation, select the Place as Landscape check box. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Color Profile Settings Dialog Box
text: Add, edit or delete a color profile in the list on the Adjust Image Quality/Color tab. You can add the new color profile provided by the developer to the list and use it. Color Profile: Select a color profile pattern in the list. Delete Delete the selected color profile pattern. Edit Name: The name entered here will be displayed in the Color Profile: list. Note: Enter up to 31 single-byte or 15 double-byte characters. Path/File Name: Enter a path name and file name for the color profile. Browse... Browse and select the color profile data saved on your computer. Add Add the color profile data specified and saved with a name to the Color Profile: list. Update Update the name or data you want to use for the color profile. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Creep Adjustment Dialog Box
text: You can print a document using the creep adjustment function. Adjust Creep Enter the respective widths of the inner page's center binding and outer page's center binding. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the units of measurement. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Using the Creep Adjustment Function

title: Print Crop Marks Details Dialog Box
text: Configure settings for crop marks. Length of Crop Marks: Specify the length of crop marks. First Page Only Select the check box to print crop marks to the first page only. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Edit Header/Footer Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to edit and create a header/footer. Date and Time Select a position and format in each list. Page Number Select a position and format in each list. Text Select a position and format in each list. If you select User Text in the Format: list, enter the text for the header/footer in the Text: box using up to 32 single-byte or 16 double-byte characters. Font: Select a font type for the header and footer text. Size: Specify a value in this spin box to adjust the size of the current header and footer text. Per Original Page Prints header/footer on each original page even when Layout or Booklet setting is applied. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Set Image Position Dialog Box
text: Make the print image position settings. Image Position: Select the print image position. Adjust Image Position Select the direction you want to move the print position. Enter the value you want to increase the margin widths of the left or right margin and the top or bottom margin according to the selected direction. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the units of measurement. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Binding Margins for 2 sided Printing Dialog Box
text: Specify the widths of the binding margins for 2 sided printing. Adjust Binding Margins Enter each width of the front and back binding margins. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the units of measurement. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Rotate Mixed Original Orientation Dialog Box
text: When documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages are printed, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are printed rotated by 90 degrees. Click to select the direction to which you want to rotate those pages. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Printout Result: Select a printout result. Printer Defaults When applying 2 sided printing or stapling, use this setting to specify the print direction settings correctly. Rotate to a naturally readable direction Landscape pages within portrait documents are rotated by 90 degrees leftward for printing. Likewise, portrait pages within landscape documents are rotated by 90 degrees rightward. Rotate to reverse readable direction Landscape pages within portrait documents are rotated by 90 degrees rightward for printing. Likewise, portrait pages within landscape documents are rotated by 90 degrees leftward. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Mixed Original Orientations: Booklet Dialog Box
text: When applying booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, you can specify whether to print document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation rotated by 90 degrees or reduced in size without being rotated. Printout Result: Specify a printout result when you apply booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages. Rotate to a Naturally Readable Direction When you apply booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are not changed, but rotated to a naturally readable direction. Reduce without Rotation When you apply booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are not rotated, but reduced so they can be printed in the same direction. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Mixed Original Orientations: Layout Dialog Box
text: When applying layout-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, you can specify whether to print document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation rotated by 90 degrees or reduced in size without being rotated. Printout Result: Specify a printout result when you apply layout-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages. Rotate to same orientation as original Document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are not changed, but rotated to a naturally readable direction. Reduce without Rotation Document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are not rotated, but reduced so they can be printed in the same direction. Page Break Creates blank pages so document pages of different orientation are not included. Note: This setting is automatically selected when an item other than Printer Defaults is selected in the Rotate Mixed Original Orientation dialog box opened from the Output Settings menu. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Register Image Overlay Dialog Box
text: Register form data for image overlay print. Registration Number: Enter a registration number for the image overlay. Registration Name: Enter a registration name for the image overlay. Image Overlay Orientation: Select the orientation of paper for the image overlay. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Edit Overlay Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to edit and create Overlay Setting. Use an ".rpo" Overlay Data file. Note: To print the same Overlay Data using different setting configurations, provide each of the available data combinations with its own overlay data name and register those names in advance. Overlay Data: Select an Overlay Setting that you want to edit or delete from the list. Delete Deletes the current Overlay Setting. Edit Name: Enter a name for the Overlay Setting. Path/File Name: Enter the path and file name for the Overlay Data file. Browse... Browse for the file you want to use as Overlay Data. Add Adds an edited Overlay Setting as a new Overlay Setting to the list. Update Saves the changes after editing an Overlay Setting. Bring to Front Select the check box to move the Overlay Data to the front. The text under the Overlay Data will not be visible. First Page Only Select the check box to superimpose the Overlay Data on only the first page of a document. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Overlaying Printing Documents with Data

title: Paper Type in Bypass Tray Dialog Box
text: Paper Type in Bypass Tray: Select the type of paper placed on the bypass tray. Note: If you select Plain & Recycled (Auto. for Postcard) , it is normally printed as plain paper/recycled paper. If the print paper size is postcard, print with a paper type suitable for postcards. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Data Security for Copying Details Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to make settings for the Data Security for Copying function. To open this dialog box, select Data Security for Copying in Unauthorized Copy Prevention Type on the Effects menu, and then select Details... . If a document with embedded copy guard pattern is copied, scanned, and/or stored in the machine with the Copy Data Security unit, the image of the page to be printed is destroyed, and turn the copy's color completely gray. Note: Depending on the data security for copying settings, the driver's prevention pattern may be overwritten by the printer's pattern. Copy Guard Text Print Image Displays an image of the data security for copying text print. Note: The images for Layout: , 2 sided: , Booklet: , and Poster: may not be displayed. Text Type: Select the text type for the data security for copying text in the list. Enter User Text: If you select User Text in Text Type: , enter a user text using up to 64 single-byte characters. Font: Select the font type for the data security for copying text. Only TrueType fonts are available. Font Style: Select the font style. Size: Specify a value to adjust the size of the data security for copying text. Note: If you use a small font, it may not be effective for the data security for copying. A font size of over 50 points is effective, and 70 to 80 points is recommended. Angle: Specify a value in this spin box to rotate the data security for copying text about its central point. Note: An Angle of 30 to 40 degrees is effective for the data security for copying text and is recommended. Position: Select a position to enter the data security for copying text in the list. Repeat: Print the prevention text string repeatedly from the top left of the page. Position: is not available. Line Space: Specify the line spacing. Outlined Prints the text in outline form. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Using Data Security for Copying Function (Destroy the Image and Print gray)

title: Toner Save User Settings Dialog Box
text: Specify the settings for each component. Text: Specify the amount of toner used for text by specifying a percentage between 1 and 100%. Graphics: Specify the amount of toner used for graphics, tables and graphs by specifying a percentage between 1 and 100%. Photograph: Specify the amount of toner used for photographs and images by specifying a percentage between 1 and 100%. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern Details Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to make settings for the Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern function. To open this dialog box, select Unauthorized Copy Prevention for Pattern in Unauthorized Copy Prevention Type on the Effects menu, and then click Details... . Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Note: Depending on the unauthorized copy prevention settings, the driver's prevention pattern may be overwritten by the printer's pattern. Prevention Copy Pattern Print Image Displays an image of the prevention copy pattern print. Note: The images for Mask Type: may not be displayed. The images for Layout: , 2 sided: , Booklet: , and Poster: may not be displayed. Text Type: Select the text type for the Prevention Text in the list. Enter User Text: If you select User Text in Text Type: , enter a user text using up to 64 single-byte characters. Font: Select the font type for the prevention text. Only TrueType fonts are available. Font Style: Select the font style. Size: Specify a value to adjust the size of the prevention text. Note: If you use a small font, it may not be effective for the prevention copy pattern. A font size of over 50 points is effective, and 70 to 80 points is recommended. Angle: Specify a value in this spin box to rotate the prevention text about its central point. Note: An Angle of 30 to 40 degrees is effective for the prevention copy pattern and is recommended. Position: Select a position to enter the prevention text in the list. Repeat: Print the prevention text string repeatedly from the top left of the page. Position: is not available. Line Space: Specify the line spacing. Outlined Prints the text in outline form. Note: You cannot select the Text Only check box when the Outlined check box is selected. When you select the Outlined check box, the Reverse Patterns: Text/Background check box is automatically selected at the same time. Text Only Use only the text pattern when printing with the unauthorized copy prevention. This is useful when the background pattern would make the document hard to read. Note: You cannot select the Outlined check box when the Text Only check box is selected. You cannot select the check box when the Reverse Patterns: Text/Background check box is selected. You cannot select the Mask Type check box when the Text Only check box is selected. Reverse Patterns: Text/Background Exchange the pattern of the text and the pattern of the background. Note: You cannot select the Text Only check box when the Reverse Patterns: Text/Background check box is selected. Mask Type: Select the mask type for the background pattern. Note: You cannot select the Reverse Patterns: Text/Background check box when a mask type is selected. You cannot select the Text Only check box when a mask type is selected. Density: Select the density of the prevention copy text/pattern. Color: Select the color that the background text and pattern will print in. No Pattern Area: Exclude the specified area from being printed with the pattern. Use this function for the area such as bar codes. Specify the values for A:top , B:bttm , C:left , and D:right in mm. The specified range is 1-9999 mm. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Using Unauthorized Copy Prevention Function (Effects of Prevention for Pattern)

title: Fine-tuning the Printable Area
text: Use the following procedure to adjust the printable area. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the type of draw area in the Printable Area: list. If you select Maximum , print inside the 5 mm (0.2 inches) margin around the paper edges, the quality might be reduced. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Adjusting the Print Image on the Paper Use the following procedure to adjust the image position. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Click Set Image Position... to open the Set Image Position dialog box. Select the print position in the Image Position: list. In the Adjust Image Position area, select the direction in which you want to shift the print area in the Direction: list. Change the margins (top, bottom, left, right) according to the selected direction. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Using the Creep Adjustment Function
text: You can print a document using the creep adjustment function. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. What Is "Creep"? When using the Magazine format to perform 2 sided printing the entire stack is folded in half, which makes the binding area more difficult to see the further the pages are from center. The Creep function lets you narrow the binding area of center pages and widen the binding area of outer pages, making the binding area of the outer pages more visible . 1. Width of inner page's center binding 2. Width of outer page's center binding Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Select Booklet: on the Frequently Used Settings tab. You can also select it on the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select Magazine in the Booklet: list. Select the document orientation in the Page Order: list. Configure the setting for printing mixed orientation documents if necessary. Open the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab if the Frequently Used Settings tab is displayed. Click the Mixed Original Orientations... button to open the dialog box. For Rotate Mixed Original Orientation of the Output Settings menu, select Printer Defaults . Specify whether to print document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation rotated by 90 degrees or reduced in size without being rotated. Click OK to close the dialog box. Open the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu of the Detailed Settings tab if the Frequently Used Settings tab is displayed. Click the Creep Adjustment... button to open the dialog box. Specify the binding margins for Inside Pages: and Outside Pages: . The margin to adjust is the length from the center line, not the length from left to right across the center line. Select inch or mm as the units of measurement in the Measurement Unit: list. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing a Document with Crop Marks
text: You can print a document with crop marks applied. This function is useful to print a document that has edges you want to trim off. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. What are Crop Marks? Crop marks are line markings for trimming documents. Crop marks are printed on front sides when 2 sided printing is applied. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Output Settings menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Print Crop Marks check box. Click Details... . The Print Crop Marks Details dialog box appears. Specify the length of the crop marks in Length of Crop Marks: . Select the First Page Only when printing crop marks on the first page only. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing a Document with a Header and Footer
text: Text inserted in the top margin of each page of a document is called a header, and text inserted in the bottom margin is called a footer. Besides date, page number, and file name, text of up to 16 double-byte or 32 single-byte characters can be inserted into these areas. Note: If you print a document using the Reduce/Enlarge function, the header and footer will also be reduced or enlarged. A header and footer will be printed on every page. For example, if you print several document pages on a sheet of paper (Layout), a header and footer will appear on every page. If you want to print a header and footer on every sheet but not every page, clear the Per Original Page check box. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Header/Footer check box. Select the items that you want to print on header and footer, Date and Time , Page Number , and Text . To edit the header and footer items, click Details... to open the Edit Header/Footer dialog box. In the Date and Time group, select a position and a format for printing date and time. In the Page Number group, select a position and a format for printing page number. In the Text group, select a position and a format for printing text. If you select User Text in the Format: list, enter the text for header/footer in the Text: box using up to 32 single-byte or 16 double-byte characters. Specify a font and font size in Font: and Size: . To print header and footer per page of document, select the Per Original Page check box. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Registering Image Overlay
text: If the hard disk is installed on the printer, you can create and register image overlays. What Is Image Overlay? This function allows you to create form data that is usable with page frames, so you can make settings for combining and printing documents. For details about using image overlay, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Note: Printing is not possible using this driver; only image overlay registration can be performed. For details about print-capable emulations, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Use Web Image Monitor to confirm or delete registered image overlay settings. For details, see the Web Image Monitor help. Always return to normal printing after registering an image overlay. Always return to a resolution of 600 dpi, regardless of the driver setting. The toner save function may become invalid. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating frame data for use in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select Store as Image Overlay in the Job Type: list. Click the Details... button to open the Register Image Overlay dialog box. Enter a number for the image overlay in Registration Number: . Enter a number between 1 and 300. Registration is cancelled if you enter a number that is already registered. To register a new image overlay with an existing number, use Web Image Monitor to delete the first registration. Enter a name for the image overlay in Registration Name: . You can enter up to 64 single-byte or 32 double-byte characters except double quotation marks. Select an orientation in the Image Overlay Orientation: area. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. The image overlay data is saved on the printer's hard disk.

title: Printing Images Superimposed on Prints
text: Follow the procedure below to print an image superimposed on prints. The image is referred to as a watermark. A watermark made up of a bitmap file (extension .bmp) is referred to as an image watermark. Note: If you use this function, register the image watermarks in advance. Having Images Stamped on Prints Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Add Bitmap check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. Enter a name for a new watermark in the Name: box. To edit a registered watermark, select the watermark in the Bitmap: list. In the Path/File Name: box, specify the path and file name for the bitmap data. Alternatively, Browse... to select the bitmap data you want to use. Select the position where you want to print the watermark in the Position: list. To adjust the size for the watermark, specify a value in the Size: spin box. To print the watermark on the first page only, select the First Page Only check box. To place the watermark over the document, select the Opaque check box. The document under the watermark will not be visible. To print watermarks repeatedly, select the Repeat check box. To print watermarks on each original page when Layout or Booklet setting is applied, select the Per Original Page check box. After specifying the settings, click Add or Update to save the watermark. If you click Update , a dialog box appears asking if you want to overwrite the old watermark. Click Yes . Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. You can select the registered image watermark in the Bitmap: list on the Effects menu. To print the same watermark data using different setting configurations, provide each of the available data combinations with its own watermark data name and register those names in advance. Deleting an Image Watermark Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Add Bitmap check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. Select a watermark from the Bitmap: list, and then click Delete . A dialog box appears prompting for confirmation. Click Yes . Click OK to close the dialog box.

title: Printing a Document with Imposition Methods
text: You can print a document using an imposition arrangement to give you the finishing you require. Trimming a printout into several pages reduces print cost. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. When Printing One Copy (Speed) For example, you print an A4 document of four pages. Two pages of the document are printed on one sheet of A3. The A3 sheets can then be cut in half and stacked to make an A4 document of four pages. In this example, four prints are produced, but the print count is only two. When Printing Plural Copies (Double) For example, you print two copies of an A4 document. Two pages of the document are printed on one sheet of A3. The A3 sheet can then be cut in half to make two copies of the A4 document. In this example, two prints are produced, but the print count is only one. Speed: Double: Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Imposition menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select the imposition method from the Imposition (Speed): or Imposition (Double): list. The icons show the available page flows of the imposition type selected. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Changing the Page Rotation Direction for Mixed Orientation Documents
text: Some applications allow the page size and orientation of a single document to be changed. When documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages are printed, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are printed rotated by 90 degrees. You can change the direction in which the images are rotated. Note: If you select Printer Defaults , you can specify the print direction settings even when layout-printing or booklet-printing is selected in the 2 Sided/Layout/Booklet menu. When you apply layout-printing or booklet-printing to documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are rotated or not rotated but reduced in size. Therefore, no blank pages are output. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Output Settings menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Click Rotate Mixed Original Orientation... to open the Rotate Mixed Original Orientation dialog box. Select Printer Defaults , Rotate to a naturally readable direction , or Rotate to reverse readable direction . Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Selecting the Paper Tray
text: When Auto Tray Select is selected, a paper tray containing paper of the appropriate size and type will be selected automatically. However, if several paper trays are loaded with paper of the same size, your document might not be printed on the paper you intend. To make sure that the correct paper is selected, you can specify the tray containing paper to print onto before printing. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Paper menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Input Tray: list, select the paper tray containing the paper you want to print onto. If Bypass Tray is selected, click the Position in bypass tray... button to open the printing preferences dialog box. Select the direction of paper loaded in the bypass tray. Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Setting Up Options

title: Overlaying Printing Documents with Data
text: A document created in an application will be superimposed with the Overlay Data created separately, and then printed. This function is called Overlay. For printing with the Overlay function, an Overlay Data file and Overlay Setting must be created in advance. 1. Overlay Data: This is the image data for superimposing, which is saved in the Overlay format. 2. Overlay Setting: An Overlay Data file is combined with the setting details (such as how and which page Overlay Data is superimposed on), named, and registered as a set. Each set registered is called an Overlay Setting. When printing with Overlay, select an Overlay Setting with the setting details, and the method and page that you prefer the image to be superimposed on. 3. A document to be printed: Using an application, create a document to be printed with the Overlay Setting. 4. Print result: The document is printed with the Overlay Setting. Superimposing data will be aligned with the document page at the upper left corner. If the document to be printed and superimposing data differ in size and orientation, the superimposing data might be cut or protrude. Depending on the application, you might not get the expected result. Creating a New Overlay Data File Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Job Setup menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select Save as Overlay Data in the Job Type: list. Click Details... to open a dialog box and select the destination to save the overlay data. Enter the file name for the "rpo" overlay data file. Click Save to save the new overlay data and close the dialog box. Overlaying Printing Documents with Overlay Data Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Add Overlay check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. Enter the name of the Overlay Setting in the Name: box. To edit a registered Overlay Setting, select the name of the overlay setting in the Overlay Data: list. In the Path/File Name: box, enter the path and file name for the Overlay Data file or click Browse... to select the file you want to use as the Overlay Data . To print the Overlay Data in the front, select the Bring to Front check box. The image under the Overlay Data will not be visible. To superimpose the Overlay Data on the first page only, select the First Page Only check box. After specifying the settings, click Add or Update to save the setting. If you click Update , a dialog box appears asking if you want to overwrite the old overlay setting. Click Yes . Click OK to close the dialog box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. You can select a registered Overlay Setting in the Overlay Data: list on the Effects menu. To print the same overlay data using different setting configurations, provide each of the available data combinations with its own overlay data name and register those names in advance. Deleting an Overlay Setting Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Effects menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Add Overlay check box. Click Edit... to open a dialog box. Select an Overlay Setting from the Overlay Data: list, and then click Delete . A dialog box appears prompting for confirmation. Click Yes . Click OK to close the dialog box.

title: Displaying the Preview Screen before Printing
text: You can display the preview screen to check before printing. You can also change some of the settings on the preview screen. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: This function is available only if you have already installed Ridoc Desk Navigator, Ridoc Desk Navigator Lt, or Ridoc IO Navi. For details about the settings, see the Help files for Ridoc Desk Navigator, Ridoc Desk Navigator Lt, or Ridoc IO Navi. Displaying the preview screen with this function may take longer than normal printing. Using this function may also cause your computer to run slowly. This function may not be available in a "Point and Print" environment. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Driver Options menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Display Preview and Print Screen check box. Click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. The preview screen appears. Check the preview screen. Change settings as necessary. For details about preview screen settings, see the Help files for Ridoc Desk Navigator, Ridoc Desk Navigator Lt, or Ridoc IO Navi. Click Print to close the preview screen.

title: Printing a Scanned Data on a Standard Size of Paper
text: When a document is scanned for printing, its size might be detected as larger than the original, and a printer error might occur. This function prevents this problem. Note: If a custom paper size is selected in the Document Size: list on the Basic menu, it is automatically changed to A4. If a custom paper size is selected in Print On: , it is automatically changed to Same as Original Size . Open the printing preferences dialog box after opening a scanned document from an application. Click the Driver Options menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Near Standard Size check box. Select a standard size in the Document Size: list on the Basic menu. You can also select from the Frequently Used Settings tab. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing in Two Colors
text: Use the following procedure to print with black and one of CMY color toners. This method is useful when you want to improve the readability of documents or to emphasize specific points, except when printing data with photographs, which should be left true to the original. Printing in two colors saves printing costs and enables document creation with effective usage of colors. If you want to print with only specific CMYK color(s), use the Separate into CMYK, then Print in Designated Color Only function. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Example: When Black & Cyan is selected Note: This function is unavailable with black and white printers. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Color in the Color/ Black and White: list. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings in the Adjust Image Quality/Color . Select a combination of toners to be used for printing in Two-color: list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Upgrading the Printer Driver
text: When upgrading the printer driver, uninstall the old version before installing the new one. Uninstalling the Printer Driver This describes how to uninstall the printer driver and delete any custom settings registered. If you want to use any existing custom settings after the upgrade, save them as a printer properties settings file before you start. For details about saving and registering One Click Preset, see Saving a Registered One Click Preset as a File and Loading a Printing Preferences Settings File as a One Click Preset . In the Devices and Printers window, select the icon of the printer you want to delete. Right click the selected printer icon, and then click Remove device . If multiple drivers are registered on one printer icon, click Delete print queue and select the driver to delete. When a confirmation message appears, click Yes . The printer icon is deleted. Select a printer icon, and then click Print server properties . On the Drivers tab in the Print Server Properties dialog box, select the printer you want to delete, and then click Remove... . Restart Windows. Installing the New Printer Driver In the Devices and Printers window, click Add a printer . Follow the instructions given by the printer wizard. When the dialog box asking for the machine manufacturer and model appears, click Have Disk... and specify the directory containing the new printer driver files. When you are asked to keep the existing driver or to replace the existing driver with the new driver, click Replace existing driver . When installation is completed, restart Windows. Configure installed options and paper trays. This is only necessary if bidirectional communication is not operating.

title: Edit Bitmap Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to edit and create bitmap watermarks. Use bitmap files (extension ".bmp") for bitmap watermarks. Note: To print the same image watermark data using different setting configurations, provide each of the available data combinations with its own image watermark name and register those names in advance. Bitmap Watermark image Displays an image of the bitmap as it appears on the page. Bitmap: Select a bitmap watermark that you want to edit or delete from the list. Delete Deletes the current watermark. Edit Configure settings for a bitmap watermark. Image data files must be 24 bits or lower bitmaps (extension ".bmp"). Name: Enter a name for the bitmap watermark. Path/File Name: Enter a path and file name for the bitmap image file. Browse... Browse for the file you want to use as bitmap watermark. Size: Specify a value in this spin box to adjust the size of the bitmap watermark. Add Adds an edited watermark as a new bitmap watermark to the list. Update Saves the changes after editing a bitmap watermark. Position: Select a printing position where you want to print the watermark. First Page Only Select the check box to print the bitmap watermark on the first page only. Opaque Select the check box to make the bitmap watermark opaque. The image under the watermark will not be visible. Repeat Prints bitmap watermarks repeatedly from the top left of the page. Per Original Page Select the check box to print the bitmap watermark on each original page even when Layout or Booklet setting is applied. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened. Printing Images Superimposed on Prints

title: Color Balance Tab
text: Use this tab to adjust brightness, contrast, saturation, and color balance. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Call Preset Call up the preset color balance. Note: When you select the preset and click the Call button, the selected color balance is reflected in the image. Edit Color Balance Setting Method Select a component for adjustment. Note: This function is available only if you select By Each Component for Setting Method . Before Displays the image of before color adjustment. After Displays the image of after color adjustment. Brightness: Specify a value in the spin box to adjust the brightness. Note: Brightness refers to the brightness of the whole image. Higher brightness levels result in a lighter print image; lower levels, in a darker print image. Contrast: Specify a value in the spin box to adjust the contrast. Note: Contrast refers to the relative contrast between light and dark parts of the print image. Higher contrast levels result in a sharper print image; lower levels, in a softer print image. Saturation: Specify a value in the spin box to adjust the saturation. Note: Saturation is the purity of a color. Increasing saturation makes a color more vivid, while decreasing saturation makes a color duller. Adjust Each Color Specify values in the spin boxes to adjust the color balance of red, green, and blue. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings.

title: Adjusting the Color Balance
text: The color balance is adjusted by changing the mixture of red (R) green (G), and blue (B). The color balance is adjusted by changing the mixture of black (K) cyan (C), magenta (M), and yellow (Y). This function is available only for color printers. Complementary Color The colors of the RGB color model can be mixed to produce the cyan, magenta, and yellow of the CMY color model and vice versa. Two colors of one model are mixed to produce the color of the other (mixing blue and green produces cyan, for example). The remaining color is the complement of the color produced (red in this example). Complementary colors are: red and cyan, green and magenta, blue and yellow. Registering the Color Balance in a User Setting Open the printing preferences dialog box. Click the Print Quality:Standard menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Advanced Settings for Adjust Image Quality/Color . Click Details... button to open the Details dialog box and click Color Balance tab. If you select Single Component for Setting Method , select the component you want to adjust from Text , Graphics , or Photograph . Specify a value in the Brightness: spin box to adjust the brightness. Specify a value in the Contrast: spin box to adjust the contrast. Specify a value in the Saturation: spin box to adjust the saturation. Specify a value in the spin box in the Adjust Each Color group to adjust the color balance of red (R), green (G), and blue (B). Click OK to save the color balance and close the dialog box. Tips for Adjusting the Color Balance The following methods are available to make a specific color stronger: decreasing the color's complementary color or decreasing the other colors (that is, decreasing complementary colors relatively). A combination of both methods can be used. For example, to make red more vivid, make it stronger (by decreasing cyan) or decrease green and blue (making magenta and yellow stronger). The more red that is used, the brighter it looks. This is useful to adjust the colors of a dark image. Conversely, the less green and blue that are used, the duller the image looks. Use this method to make a bright image dull. Example No adjustment: Increased red: Decreased green and blue:

title: Printing Eight Pages on a Sheet for Making Pamphlets
text: Use the following procedure to arrange eight pages on one sheet using a layout suitable for pamphlets. Cut and fold the sheet according to the lines to make a pamphlet. If the orientation of the first page is portrait, the pamphlet will open to the left. If it is landscape, it will open to the top. Red line: Cut line / Dotted line: Mountain fold / Solid line: Valley fold Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Splitting the Document Image across Multiple Sheets (Poster)
text: Follow the procedure below to print a single document page over multiple sheets to make a poster size print. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. 1 Page into 4 Sheets Note: The enlargement ratio used is based on the specified paper size and the number of sheets you want to split the image over. Prints are made with a 15 mm (0.6 inches) overlap margin. When pasting sheets together, overlap them to hide this margin. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Imposition menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the number of sheets you want to split the image over in the Poster: list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Adjust Image Quality/Color Tab
text: Set the image quality and color tone. Color Profile: Select a color profile pattern. If you select By Each Component , different settings can be assigned to each element of text, photographic, and presentation. Depending on the printer you are using, the available items may vary. Changing the Color Profiling Pattern Automatic Automatically configures the best color profile pattern depending on the appearance of the document to print. Automatic (Brighter) Automatically configures the best color profile pattern to be brighter. Automatic (Darker) Automatically configures the best color profile pattern to be darker. Text Optimizes the colors for text. Text (Brighter) Optimizes the colors for text to be brighter. Text (Darker) Optimizes the colors for text to be darker. Photographic Enhances mid-tone colors similar to those seen in photographs. Photographic (Brighter) Enhances mid-tone colors, similar to those seen in photographs, to be brighter. Photographic (Darker) Enhances mid-tone colors, similar to those seen in photographs, to be darker. Presentation Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics. This setting is best for printing tables, graphs, and presentation materials that contain color. Presentation (Brighter) Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics to be brighter. Presentation (Darker) Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics to be darker. CAD Enhances reproduction of even colors that are true to the original. POP Display Prints the color red more vividly. It is an optimal setting for the POP display. Color Variation 1 (Bright/Yellow) Enhances colors suitable for portraits. Color Variation 2 (Dark/Red) Enhances colors suitable for portraits or food. Color Variation 3 (Darker/Blue) Prints the color blue more vividly. Suitable for landscapes. Color Variation 4 (Dark/Yellow) Enhances dark-tone colors over the whole area. Color Variation 5 (Brighter/Red) Enhances bright-tone colors over the whole area. Color Variation 6 (Brighter/Yellow) Enhances brightness and contrast over the whole area. Color Variation 7 (Darker/Red) Enhances dark-tone colors and contrast over the whole area. Off Prints colors without modification. Use ICM Corrects colors using the Windows ICM function. Using ICM Expand Gray Recognition Checks every pixel and prints gray pixels (when the values of RGB are equal or nearly equal) using black toner only. This setting is available only if you have selected K: Expand Gray Recognition in the Gray Reproduction: list. Barrier-free Color Management Converts the colors used in documents to the barrier-free colors applicable to Color Universal Design (CUD). This setting is available only if you have selected On in the Barrier-free Color Management: list. Dithering: Select a dithering pattern suitable for the document image. If you select By Each Component , different settings can be assigned to each element of text, photographic, and presentation. Depending on the printer you are using, the available items may vary. Changing the Dithering Pattern Automatic Automatically configures the best dithering method depending on the appearance of the document to print. Photographic Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for photographs. Text Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for text. Thin lines Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for thin lines. Thin colored lines can be seen easily. CAD Performs dithering using a pattern appropriate for CAD printing. Gray Reproduction: Select the printing method appropriate for black and gray areas of documents. K (Black) Prints black and gray using black toner only. Compared to the black printed with CMYK toner, this results in a black that is relatively flatter and purer. Note: Depending on the application you are using, black and gray images may print with CMYK toner even if K (Black) is selected. CMY + K Prints black and gray on all pages using four colors: CMY (Cyan, Magenta, and Yellow) and K (Black). K(Black) for Text Prints black and gray text using black toner only. K (Black) for Gray Pixels Only Checks every pixel and prints gray pixels (when the values of RGB are equal) using black toner only. Other pixels are printed using CMYK toner. K: Expand Gray Recognition Checks every pixel and prints gray pixels (when the values of RGB are equal or nearly equal) using black toner only. Note: Color Balance is set to Expand Gray Recognition . Black/Gray by K-Strong UCR Prints all black and gray objects using black toner only regardless of whether the document is in color or black and white. This is useful when a black and gray image or scanned black text might print with CMYK toner even if K (Black) is selected. Color Profile Method: Specify how to print your color graphics. By Host System A color management system (ICM) function or color matching is performed by the host computer before the document is sent to the printer. ICM is performed by the OS, and color matching by the printer driver. By Printer Color matching is performed by the printer. By Printer Driver ICM is performed by the printer driver. ICM Intent: Specify how color images are created to produce the best looking image on the printed page. Note: This function is available only if By Printer Driver is already selected in the Color Profile Method: list. Graphics (Saturation) Enhances basic colors used for text and graphics. This setting is best for printing tables, graphs, and presentation materials that contain color. Pictures (Perceptual) Enhances mid-tone colors similar to those seen in photographs. Proof (Relative Colorimetric) Renders colors in an image with the closest colors possible. This is suitable for printing colors that need to be rendered accurately, such as colors in logos. The colors that fall outside the printer color gamut will be rendered to the closest color possible. Match (Absolute Colorimetric) Assuming a device-independent color space, this provides a wider range of colors than the printer color gamut. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this tab to the default settings.

title: User Authentication Dialog Box
text: If the user authentication settings have been made on the printer, you also need to make the user authentication settings on the printer driver. After selecting the User Authentication to On , enter a login name and password in the Authentication dialog box on the Basic tab. Using User Authentication Note: For details about user authentication, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. User Authentication Select On to print using user authentication. Display [Authentication] Dialog Before Print Select this check box to display the Authentication dialog box before printing. After you enable the function, select whether to display a dialog box every time or to display it only when Login User Name is blank. Reenter the Confirmation Key: Enter the login password again for confirmation. Note: The optional network data protection unit must be installed. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Job Type/Code Dialog Settings Dialog Box
text: Set whether to display a confirmation dialog box before printing starts. Display [Classification Code] Dialog Before Printing Select the check box to display the Classification Code dialog box before printing. Display [User Code] Dialog Before Printing Select the check box to display the User Code dialog box before printing. title: Security Settings Dialog Box
text: Set whether to encrypt print data. Encrypt Data for Locked Print, Stored Print, and Stored Print (Shared) Selecting this check box encrypts print data before sending it to the printer. If Password is NOT Entered Set whether to cancel printing if a password is not entered in the Change Job Type dialog box when encrypting data. OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Cover/Slip/Designate
text: Use this menu to make settings for covers, slip sheets, or chapter pages. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Front Cover Prints the first page on a slip sheet or inserts a blank sheet as the front cover. Printing Only the First Sheet on a Different Type of Paper Input Tray: Select the tray containing the paper to use for the front cover. Print Mode: Select one of the options for the cover. Leave Blank The cover sheet is not printed on. Printing begins on the second sheet. One Side Only one side of the cover sheet is printed on. If you have specified 2 sided printing, selecting this will ensure only one side of the cover sheet is printed on. Both Sides Both sides of the cover sheet are printed on. This option is available only for 2 sided printing. Paper Type in Bypass Tray... Specify the type of printing medium you want to use when using bypass tray paper as the front cover sheet. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Back Cover Prints the last page on a slip sheet or inserts a blank sheet as the back cover. Printing the Back Cover on a Different Type of Paper Input Tray: Select the tray containing the paper to use for the back cover. Note: Depending on the printer you use, the input tray selected for the front cover may be always used for the last sheet. In this case, the Input Tray: list is unavailable. Print Mode: Select one of the options for the back cover. Depending on the printer you are using, the available items may vary. Leave Blank The back cover sheet is not printed on. Print on Back Cover Prints on the back cover sheet. Print on Outer Back Cov. Prints on the back side of the back cover sheet. Paper Type in Bypass Tray... Specify the type of printing medium you want to use when using bypass tray paper as the back cover sheet. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Insert Slip Sheet After Every Page Inserts a separator sheet after every printed sheet. Inserting Different Paper between Pages Input Tray: Select the tray containing the paper to use for the slip sheets. Note: The slip sheet function is not available if the same input trays are selected for both print pages and slip sheets. Print Mode: Select whether or not to print on slip sheets. Depending on the printer you are using, the available items may vary. Leave Blank Inserts a blank sheet as a separator. Print on Slip Sheet Prints on slip sheets. Paper Type in Bypass Tray... Specify the type of printing medium you want to use when using bypass tray paper as the slip sheet. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Designate/Chapter You can divide a document into chapters and print the first page of each chapter on different paper. You can also select the print mode for the first page of each chapter. (Designate/Chapter) In addition, you can print the selected pages on different paper. (Designated Sheet Print) Using Designate/Chapter Function Details... Opens the Designate/Chapter Details dialog box where you can configure the detailed settings.

title: Output Settings
text: Use this menu to make settings for output tray or to specify how you want to have prints delivered to the output tray. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Output Tray: Specify an output tray. If you select Printer Default , prints are delivered to the output tray specified on the printer. Collate: Sorts the prints into sets when multiple sets of documents are printed. Select a collate method in the list. Having Prints Sorted Printer Collate Ignores the application's collate function and applies the printer driver's collate function. Application Collate Applies the collate function set in the application's Print dialog box. Note: To apply stacking options, select Application Collate and then set the application's collate function to "OFF" in the Print dialog box. Collate Details... Opens the Collate Details dialog box, where you can select a collate type. Rotate Mixed Original Orientation... When documents containing a mixture of landscape and portrait pages are printed, document pages whose orientation differs from the paper orientation are rotated by 90 degrees. You can change the direction in which the images are rotated. Reverse Order Printing When this check box is selected, the document starts printing from the last page. Use this function when prints come out face up in the output tray. Note: If the application you are using has a similar function, do not make settings with the application's function. If you use this function when applying 2 sided printing to a document with an odd number of pages, the blank last page will also be included in the print count. Eject Face-up Select this to deliver printed documents print side up. Use this function with Reverse Order Printing to output a printed document in page order. Printing a Document Face Up Note: This function might not be available depending on the folding type you selected in the Fold: list. Print Crop Marks Prints crop marks on each page. Details... Configure settings for crop marks. Enable [Stamp] in Printer Settings on the Device Select the check box to print stamps registered in the device. If you want to print documents without the stamp, do not click the check box. Note: For details about the stamp setting on the device, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Insert Separation Sheet Select the check box to insert a separation sheet after every set of collated copies. To insert a separator after every two or more sets of copies instead, select the number of sets in the spin box. Input Tray: Select an input tray.

title: Designate/Chapter Details Dialog Box
text: Use this dialog box to specify the detailed settings for the Designate/Chapter function. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Page Number: Enter the page number on which a new chapter begins. If you specify the page range, use a hyphen between page numbers. If you enter multiple numbers, use a comma to separate entries. Note: The Designate/Chapter function is unavailable within the specified range of pages on the specified paper. Print Mode: Select one of the print mode options for the pages specified in Page Number: . Depending on the printer you are using, the available items may vary. Designate: Leave Blank Inserts a blank sheet as a separator from a different tray selected in Input Tray: before the page specified in Page Number: . Designate: One Side Prints the page specified in Page Number: on a chapter cover from the tray selected in Input Tray: . If you enable this setting, sheets will be printed on the front side only, even if you have specified 2 sided printing. Designate: Both Sides Prints the page specified in Page Number: on the front side of a chapter cover from a different tray selected in Input Tray: and the next page on the back side. This option is for 2 sided printing. Chapter Prints the page specified in Page Number: on the front side of the sheet at all times while in 2 sided print mode. With this selection, you will be unable to use a different input tray setting than the other pages. Designated Sheet Print Prints the specified range of pages on different sheets of paper. Input Tray: Select the tray containing the paper to use for the chapter covers. Paper Type in Bypass Tray: Specify the type of printing medium you want to use when using bypass tray paper for Designate/Chapter. Available media types differ depending on the printer you are using. Note: If you select Plain & Recycled (Auto. for Postcard) , it is normally printed as plain paper/recycled paper. If the print paper size is postcard, print with a paper type suitable for postcards. Add Click this to add your specifications of Print Mode: , Page Number: and Input Tray: to the Designate/Chapter Settings List: . Modify Click this to change a setting in Designate/Chapter Settings List: . Designate/Chapter Settings List: Lists the print modes specified for the chapter covers and their corresponding pages. Delete Click this to remove an unnecessary item after selecting it in Designate/Chapter Settings List: . Delete All Click this to delete all the items in Designate/Chapter Settings List: . OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Imposition
text: Use this menu to make settings for printing a single document page over multiple sheets. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Poster: Prints a single document page printed over multiple sheets. Splitting the Document Image across Multiple Sheets (Poster) Pamphlet: Arranges eight pages on one sheet using a layout suitable for pamphlets. Cut and fold the sheet according to the lines to make a pamphlet. Printing Eight Pages on a Sheet for Making Pamphlets Draw Border Select the check box to have document pages delineated by a dotted line. Imposition (Speed): Prints two pages of a document side by side on one sheet of paper. The sheet can then be cut in half and stacked in the specified order (left to right/right to left/top to bottom) to make one copy of a document. Printing a Document with Imposition Methods Imposition (Double): Prints two copies of a document side by side on one sheet of paper. The sheet can then be cut in half to make two copies of a document. Printing a Document with Imposition Methods

title: Manage One Click Preset List Dialog Box (Printer Properties)
text: You can change the one click preset display order, delete one click preset, and change their names and comments. You can also share registered one click presets among users. Down Moves the one click preset display order down. Delete Deletes the selected one click preset. Restore... Restores the system-provided one click presets.
