OK Saves the changes and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Perfect Binding Details Dialog Box
text: This allows you to configure the settings for Perfect Binding. Perfect binding is a binding method that applies heated glue to printed sheets to form a book block, encloses the book block in a cover sheet, and trims away excess paper to create neat edges. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Note: For details about perfect binding and the supported paper types and sizes, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Binding Position: Select the binding position. Binding Paper Source Tray: Select the paper tray from which the cover sheets will be fed. Perfect Binding Cutting Options: Select the type of cutting (edge trimming) method to apply when finishing. Do not Cut No cut is applied. Edges are not trimmed. Fore Edge (Finishing Size) Only the fore edge is trimmed. Specify the fore edge's finishing size length in the Adjust Cut Position area. Fore Edge Only the fore edge is trimmed. Specify the cut length in the Adjust Cut Position area. 3 Edges (Finishing Size) All edges except the binding edge are trimmed. Specify the finishing size in the Perfect Binding Finishing Size: list. If you select Custom Paper Size , specify the size for I. Width: and H. Length: in the Adjust Cut Position area. If you want to shift the cut position along the binding edge, specify in J. Along Binding Edge: the distance by which to shift the cut position from the center. 3 Edges All edges except the binding edge are trimmed. Specify the cut lengths for E. Head Edge: , F. Tail Edge: , and G. Fore Edge: in the Adjust Cut Position area. Measurement Unit: Select inch or mm as the measurement unit. Adjust Image Position Specify the distance by which you want to shift the print image on the book block. C. Along Binding Edge: Specify the distance by which to shift the print image along the binding edge. D. Across Binding Edge: Specify the distance by which to shift the print image across the binding edge. Adjust Cut Position Specify settings according to the cutting (edge trimming) method selected in the Perfect Binding Cutting Options: list. The shaded settings are unavailable. E. Head Edge: Specify the cut length of the head edge. F. Tail Edge: Specify the cut length of the tail edge. G. Fore Edge: Specify the cut length of the fore edge. H. Page Length: Specify the fore edge's finishing size length. Perfect Binding Finishing Size: Specify the finishing size in the list. I. Width: Specify the size of page width for the custom paper size. H. Length: Specify the size of page length for the custom paper size. J. Along Binding Edge: If you want to shift the cut position along the binding edge, specify the distance by which to shift the cut position from the center. OK Saves the entries and closes the dialog box. Cancel Closes the dialog box without saving any changes. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this dialog box to the default settings. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Print Quality:Advanced
text: Use this menu to adjust the advanced settings that can affect the output quality of the print jobs. Available functions differ depending on the printer or printer driver you are using. Restore Defaults Restores the settings on this menu to the default settings. Separate into CMYK, then Print in Designated Color Only Normally full color (CMYK) is used for color printing. However, you can choose to use only specific CMYK color(s). Printing a Document Using Only Specific CMYK Colors Vector/Raster: Specify how document data are printed. The printer driver can send document data as either raster or vector graphic images. All data can be printed as raster images, but most geometric shapes and patterns print faster as vector images. Vector Sends document data to the printer as a mixture of vector and raster images. Note: Not all images can be printed using Vector. If you select Vector and the images do not print as they appear on the computer screen, select Raster and reprint the document. Raster Sends all document data to the printer as raster images. Line Width Adjustment This function adjusts the thickness of the lines, such as in figures, in dot units. Print All Text as Black Prints all text in the print job in black regardless of the original color. Black Over Print This function allows black printing on a colored background and helps prevent misregistration. Use this function if your document features black graphics and/or text on a colored background. Overprinting Black on a Background Color (Black over print) Adjust Photographs Corrects the color tone of images taken with a digital camera. Edge Smoothing Improves the quality of text and graphics by smoothing jagged outer edges to enhance the appearance of curved lines. If you are printing a document that features images containing fine gradations of tone such as photographs, leave this check box unselected. Fuser Setting: If residual gloss appears on the same page or the next page, select High Quality . High Quality may reduce productivity. If residual gloss does not appear, select Normal . Change Data Processing Depending on the application, there may be cases where printing takes a long time, or colors are not reproduced correctly. In this kind of situation, selecting this may rectify the problem. Since selecting this may cause printing not to function correctly with some applications, you should normally leave this option unselected. Shift Shading Pattern Select the check box if the shading pattern appears faint when printing is performed. Enlarge Shading Pattern Select the check box if the pattern colors are not printed correctly as the dithering and brush effects interfere. Bold Text Adjustment Prints bold-faced characters even bolder. Make Text Thick This function increases the thickness of the font to be printed by 1 dot.

title: Register Current Settings as One Click Preset Dialog Box
text: You can register the current settings as a one click preset with its name and comment. The icon is displayed on the registered one click preset. Note: You cannot register new one click presets if the Administrator prohibits users from registering them. One Click Preset Name: Enter a name for the new one click preset. The name can be up to 128 single-byte or 64 double-byte characters. Comment: Enter a comment for the new one click preset. The comment can be up to 512 single-byte or 256 double-byte characters. You can insert line breaks. OK Saves the entries and closes the dialog box. Cancel Cancels the entries. Help Displays Help for the dialog box opened.

title: Printing on Custom Size Paper
text: Use the following procedure to print with a custom paper size. Note: A paper size mismatch error may occur due to a miscalculation in the paper size. Printing on Custom Size Paper Whose Size Has Not Been Registered Yet Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Click Custom Paper Size... to open the dialog box. Click the << Collapse list button if the Custom Paper Size... button on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. Enter the length and width of the paper as seen in the graphic. Enter the size of the paper edge that is vertical relative to the feed direction of the printer in Width: . Enter the size of the paper edge that is horizontal relative to the feed direction of the printer in Length: . Click OK to close the dialog box. Place paper on a tray compatible with the custom paper size. Returning back to your computer, make any other necessary settings, and then click OK . The printing preferences dialog box closes. Start printing. Printing on Registered Custom Size Paper Preparation: Register the size of custom size paper that is loaded in the printer properties dialog box in advance. For details, see Registering Custom Paper Sizes . Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. In the Document Size: list, select the size of custom size paper you want to print on. The custom paper sizes available in the list are those that have been registered in advance. Place paper on a tray compatible with the custom paper size. Returning back to your computer, make any other necessary settings, and then click OK . The printing preferences dialog box closes. Start printing.

title: Printing with the Folding Unit
text: You can use the optional folding unit to fold your prints as they come out. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: If the Fold: list is grayed out, check that the optional folding unit is installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab. Available fold type changes according to paper orientation, 2 sided setting, and stapling position. The folding function is not available for certain paper sizes and media types. For details, see the operating instructions provided with the printer. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Finishing menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the fold type in the Fold: list. If necessary, select the Multi-sheet Fold check box. Depending on the combination of fold type and print side that you have selected, this function might not be available. After making any additional settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Saving on Ink When Printing
text: If your printer supports an ink saving function, the following describes how you can save on ink. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Print Quality menu on the Detailed Settings tab. In the Ink Save: list, select On . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Punching Prints
text: When a printer is equipped with a finisher that has the punch function, holes can be punched in the printed documents. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Note: If the Punch: list is grayed out, check that the optional finisher is installed on the printer and selected on the Accessories tab of the printer properties dialog box. If the punch position you require is not available, check the type of punch unit selected in the Punch Unit: list on the Accessories tab. Available punch positions depend on the settings selected in Orientation and Print On: on the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Check these settings in advance. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Finishing menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Select the punching position in the Punch: list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Reducing and Enlarging a Document Size
text: Reducing and Enlarging by Specifying a Ratio Use the following procedure to reduce or enlarge the print image by specifying a percentage between 25 and 400% (adjustable in steps of 1%). Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Basic menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select Zoom or Directional Magnification in the Reduce/Enlarge: list. If Zoom is selected, specify a reduction/enlargement percentage by using the spin box of Zoom: . This ratio can be adjusted in steps of 1%. If Directional Magnification is selected, specify horizontal and vertical ratios separately using the spin boxes of Vertical: and Horizontal: . After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing. Reducing and Enlarging to Match the Specified Paper Size Use the following procedure to reduce or enlarge a document to fit it to a specified paper size. The enlargement/reduction ratio is automatically determined based on the original size and paper size you specify. This method is useful when reducing or enlarging from and to standard paper sizes, for example, reducing an A3 document onto A4 paper. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Frequently Used Settings tab or the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. Make sure that the original orientation and document size of the Document Size: list are identical to those set in the application. Usually the application settings are reflected here, but some settings may not depend on the application. If different, change these settings so that they are identical to those set from the application. Click the << Collapse list button if the Document Size: list on the Frequently Used Settings tab is not displayed. If the Frequently Used Settings tab is open, make sure that Fit to Print Size in Reduce/Enlarge: is displayed under the print image. If not, select Fit to Print Size in the Reduce/Enlarge: list on the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab. If the Basic menu of the Detailed Settings tab is open, select Fit to Print Size in the Reduce/Enlarge: list. Select the physical paper size you want to print on from the Print On: list. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start printing.

title: Printing a Document Face Up
text: You can print a document face up. Use this function with Reverse Order Printing to output a printed document in page order. When printing on label paper, this function prevents jamming as a result of the separator being taken off. If you use Eject Face-up with Reverse Order Printing , print results are as follows: This example uses a document with three pages printed. Depending on the printer you are using, this function may not be available. Reverse Order Printing Eject Face-up Print result Print status Off Off Printed on the back side of the sheets in descending order. Off On Printed on the front side of the sheets in descending order. On Off Printed on the back side of the sheets in ascending order. On On Printed on the front side of the sheets in ascending order. Open the printing preferences dialog box after creating a document in an application. Click the Output Settings menu on the Detailed Settings tab. Select the Eject Face-up check box. After making any other necessary settings, click OK to close the printing preferences dialog box. Start the print job.
